- **Questions for "main" (R10.T9.a)** (asked on issue #52).
  - _The grid's origin_ (S3). Light coordinates of a body-fixed point, measured from the body's
    centre, are the same numbers in the body-fixed basis and in the non-rotating one, since S4's
    basis turns with the body about its pole (x_L · p = (R x_L) · (R p)). So the grid slides under
    the ground by up to R δ a frame, δ the sun's turn a frame in body-fixed axes, not S3's
    3 × 10⁻⁴ m (which took δ from a 29.5-day turn and the cascade's radius as the lever, by the
    ruling's §1). On `TERRAIN TEST` at 60 s/s and 60 Hz, R δ = 126 m. Its sun stays on the
    equator (the pole is tilted about +x, normal to the sun's line), so the slide is exactly
    R δ sin e★: 11.0 m a frame with the sun 5° up (125 of cascade 1's texels), 63.2 m (714) at 30°
    and 109.4 m (1,237) at 60°. The figures asked, 9.7, 56 and 97 m, took a sun off the equator,
    which the scene does not have (the science check). On an Earth at 1 s/s, 0.67 to 6.7 m. Lean:
    an optional `gridOriginBodyFixedM` kept by T9.b near the camera. _Ruled 2026-10-20
    (decision-r10-t9-split, ruling 7 amended): carried centres, with the lattice for a first
    frame_.
  - _λ = 0.75_ (above). Lean: as built, the ruling's value, cited as the ruling's.
- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule) (R10.T9.a)** (recorded, not ruled; each leaves the
  algorithm and the contracts as built).
  - _The grid's residual crawl as the sun turns_: at most 1,024 δ texel a frame for every cascade
    (0.074 at `TERRAIN TEST`'s 60 s/s, 0.0012 on an Earth at 1 s/s), a turn about a pivot inside
    the cascade; T9.b judges it by eye (0.073 measured in the ruling's test (c)).
  - _A caller that passes no centres_ is snapped from the lattice and re-grids at each lattice face
    crossed, by under one texel on a filtered edge, and at each step of L in a descent.
  - _The pole switch_ (S4): within 1° of either pole the body-fixed +x stands in for the pole, a
    one-frame re-grid by sub-texel amounts.
  - _The radius is continuous in h_ (S8), so texels rescale through a descent; whether steps beat
    the crawl is T9.b's call by eye (MJP's sample quantises to ⌈16 r⌉ ÷ 16, a precedent). With the
    carry, a descent's texel rescaling pivots at P, at most about 1,024 ε texel a frame: about 0.2
    at h = 4 km descending at 50 m/s, and 0.35 at 500 m and 10 m/s. Measured from the body's centre
    it would be about 100 texels.
  - _The reach's cap._ Under the minimum, far casters are the horizon map's, so T9.b may measure and
    lower the cap of √(2 R Δh).
  - _A constant bias unit's world size_ (S6, S7). The brief expected it to scale with the depth
    range and so differ between the two capability paths; it does not (the science check). One unit
    is 2^(e − 23) of the range D at a caster's depth d in [2^e, 2^(e+1)), and d D is the caster's
    distance from the far plane, which stands at r from the centre on both paths. So for a caster
    in the sphere one unit is 2⁻²⁴ to 2⁻²³ of that distance on both, the same to within a factor of
    2 (1.23 to 1.55 across cascades 1 and 4 at 2 m and 4 km up); the slope term's world size is
    free of D too.
  - _Snapping's overhang._ Snapping moves a centre by up to half a texel in x_L and y_L, so the
    slice can overhang its map by that much at the edge (Microsoft's sample makes the map a texel
    larger); a point there falls to the next cascade, inside the blend band.
  - _PCF is not guaranteed._ WebGPU leaves a comparison sampler's filtering to the implementation,
    so on some adapter the 2 × 2 is a single compare and T9.b's Poisson taps carry the filtering.
  - _A cooler host's penumbra._ At the same insolation a host's disc scales as (T☉ ÷ T★)²,
    T☉ = 5,772 K (IAU 2015 B3): a 3,000 K star subtends about 2.0°, and its penumbra 10 m behind an
    occluder is about 34 cm, four of cascade 1's texels at 2 m up, so "PCSS is unneeded" holds for
    a Sun-like host; T9.b's filter may need to follow the host's angular radius.
  - _Rounding, not flooring._ Valient rounds to the nearest texel corner and Microsoft floors; both
    are whole-texel snaps, and `Math.round` is built.
  - _No receiver offset in depth._ Microsoft's sample also offsets the receiver's compared depth by
    0.002; the normal offset stands in for it here, as Holbert's method has it.
  - _SwiftShader's `depth-clip-control`._ R01's record of its engine task reads SwiftShader's
    capabilities as "no `shader-f16`, the rest present", while `platform.test.ts`'s
    `SWIFTSHADER_FEATURES` lacks the feature; T9.b's smoke run should log which path it takes, and
    withhold the feature where it is to run the pulled-back path.
  - _Pointers left for main._ The README's asks table ("met: … R10.T7, T10.d, T9.a" for the memory
    categories), plan 12's R12.T3.a (`shadows` "by R10.T7 and T9.a", and "`shadows` (R10.T9.a)")
    and this plan's Tasks opening (T9 after T8 alone) predate the split: T9.b adds `shadows`, and
    follows T9.a, T11, T12 and R10.T8.c. R10.T8.c, which T9.b's entry names, is the entry another
    change inserts above R10.T9's heading. This task edits four places of this plan alone.
- **Deviations in T10.c, as built** (2026-10-16; lane r10-shader, on `rendering-and-planets` at
  `5da24214`).
  - _Files._ In `view/terrain/`: `shaders/terrainLit.wgsl` (the discard, the skirts' and fins'
    heights, their shading), `terrainMaterial.ts` (`surveyMask` at binding 17), `slotLayout.ts`
    (`survey-mask`, `SURVEY_MASK_BYTES`, `SURVEY_CELL_CODE_BYTE`), `gpu/resources.ts`
    (`litPatchMeshData`, `LIT_VERTEX_CODE`, `SURVEY_FIN_LINES`, `LIT_PATCH_INDICES`,
    `surveyCellCode`, `packSurveyMask`, `surveyedAt`; the field's upload; the lit layout's mesh and
    index count), `terrainPass.ts` (binds the field), `coverage.ts` (`surveyEdges`, `SurveyEdge`,
    `CoverageMask.survey`), a new `surveyEdge.ts` (the mark), and `workers/{messages,heightBake}.ts`
    (`TerrainLayers.fieldLevel`). R07's `shaders/smoothMesh.wgsl` and `bodies/draw.ts`
    (`SMOOTH_MESH_MATERIAL`'s `coverageMask` at binding 13 and `coverageAxes`,
    `LitBodyInput.surveyCoverage`, `MeshBodyPlan.coverage`, `MeshBodyCoverage`); `bodies/smoothMesh.ts`
    is unchanged, the discard being its shader's. R02's `view/wireframe/drawList.ts`
    (`DrawOptions.surveyEdges`, `WireframeDrawList.surveyEdges`, `DrawnSurveyEdge`). The smoke
    harness's new `smoke/surveyEdge.ts` in `page.ts`'s part 6, and `smoke/litTerrain.ts` (binds the
    field; shares its fixture). `view/engine/types.ts`, `webgpu/materials.ts` and `platform.ts` are
    unchanged (below).
  - _The storage split was T8.b's._ `StorageBufferSpec.stages`, `stageVisibility`,
    `storageBuffersPerStage`, `resourceLayoutEntries`' per-entry visibility, the `requiredLimits` doc
    (no binding-count limit raised), `src/test/wgslStages.ts` and the counts and stage match in
    `terrainPass.test.ts` are T8.b's ("Deviations in T8.b, as built"), checked against this task's
    text and kept. This task adds the `survey-mask` field's declaration and the counts with it: the
    lit material's vertex stage reads 6 (5 on `face-differences`) and its fragment stage 4; R05's
    spike shading 5 (4) and none.
  - _The mask binds to both stages._ The fragment stage discards by it; the vertex stage reads its
    cell code alone, to stand the fins on the coarse cells' edges and fold the rest flat, which would
    otherwise raster six fins of the patch's full relief in every patch, all discarded.
  - _The discard is the coarse cell's, not the mask's half._ Design note 12's half of the
    interpolated mask stands half a quad from the cell's edge: a vertex on a cell's edge holds either
    cell's state, as the rounding of its direction falls (`PatchKey::containing`), so the half lies
    inside the surveyed cell (neither surface draws) or inside the unsurveyed one (both draw), and
    the task's smoke check fails either way. As built, a fragment reads its coarse cell's state at
    that cell's centre vertex within the patch (`survey_surveyed`, its twin `surveyedAt`), on none
    of the cell's edges, from the cell's size in quads, 2^(P + 6 − L) for a patch of level P over a
    field of level L, carried as a code in the field's spare byte 4,225 (`surveyCellCode`, log₂
    clamped to 0–6). So the terrain's edge is the cell's exactly wherever a cell spans two quads or
    more, a patch at most five levels coarser than the field; coarser still (a sixth of a face or
    more), the half of the mask between the quad's vertices stands in, as Design note 12 has it. On
    the generated world (`surveyEdge.wasm.test.ts`), over the 14 patches of levels 2 to 7 baked
    across the Moon-like fixture's first survey (a 15th, the face's root, codes 0), every quad's
    centre and the points by two of its corners read the coverage's cell exactly.
  - _Each bake carries its field's level._ `TerrainLayers.fieldLevel`, the level its mask's and
    `unsurveyedCells`' cells are of, which the worker keeps from each block's answer
    (`WorkerFields`), so that the upload can code the cell's size. A client message alone; the
    module, its golden and the wire are unchanged.
  - _The skirts and fins_ are the lit material's own mesh (`litPatchMeshData`; R05's spike and R07's
    figure keep the shared one): R05's edge skirts as each edge's foot strip, its foot at
    min(h − skirt depth, 0), still R05's crack filler and now reaching the datum from ground above
    it; a head strip over each edge vertex up to max(h, 0), rising to the datum from ground below it;
    and fins along columns and rows 16, 32 and 48, from the ground to the datum on a coarse cell's
    edge, folded flat elsewhere. The side that stands higher draws each: a surveyed cell its foot
    strips, an unsurveyed cell its head strips, a fin where its line's two cells differ; a strip
    between cells of one state lies beneath their surfaces. So no skirt needs its neighbour patch's
    survey, which a vertex on the edge cannot tell. Each triangle's first vertex names its part, read
    flat (`kind`). They are drawn in the reference surface's appearance: law 0 alone under the
    datum's normal, |μ| so either face is lit, without decoration or the horizon map, as R07's disc
    draws the reference surface. A crack between levels, which R05 closes at morph 1, now shows law
    0's colour rather than the edge vertex's.
  - _The reference surface's inverse mask._ `smoothMesh.wgsl` discards a pixel whose ray (the
    disc's `hit_spheroid` at the pixel's centre) meets the spheroid in a cell the GPU's coverage
    mask holds surveyed, its direction taken into the body's own body-fixed axes (`coverageAxes`,
    the rotation's: the figure's patches are about its pole, not the body's faces) and read as the
    disc reads a class map (`class_map_texel`). `LitBodyInput.surveyCoverage` gives the mask, which
    is ignored without a `rotation`; a body without one binds a mask of no surveyed cell (one texel
    a face), and draws as before.
  - _The GPU mask follows the workers' blocks_ (main's ruling on R10.T6.b's question):
    `CoverageMask.survey(change)` adds a block's `newlySurveyed` runs as the pool's
    `onFieldChange` reports them, and `update(coverage)` now adds the store's cells to the cells it
    holds, rather than replacing them, so that an answer behind the workers unsurveys nothing; a
    release, or a field of another level, starts it afresh.
  - _`surveyEdges(coverage, face)`._ Provides' `surveyEdges(face, level)`: the level is the
    coverage's own. Each piece (`SurveyEdge`) is a side of a surveyed cell whose neighbour across it,
    on the same face or across a face's edge (`edgeNeighbour`), is not surveyed, margin cells
    unsurveyed; each listed once, by its surveyed cell's face.
  - _The mark_ (`surveyEdgeMark`). The pieces are joined through their corners into runs, the
    surveyed cell on the left seen from outside the body; each side is drawn on the spheroid in
    pieces of at most 8 px on the view, at the rim of the step, max(drawn height, 0) (the view's
    `heightAtM`; the datum where it holds none), as view-space segments, so that a depth test hides
    it behind nearer ground, and not beyond the spheroid's horizon or behind the camera; a tick 0.25
    rem long every 1 rem of each drawn run, the first half a rem in, at right angles on the view,
    towards the unsurveyed side, its far end at its foot's depth, none within 0.5 rem of
    `options.keepClear` (the line-of-sight mark's ticks); and the range to its nearest drawn point
    inside the view, from the own ship (`options.rangeFromM`) or the camera.
    `buildWireframeDrawList` draws it from `DrawOptions.surveyEdges` in both styles, the overlay
    casing the wireframe list's lines: a batch a body, `survey-edge:<body>`, `--text` at 1 px with
    the lines' casing, never dashed, its nearest range in `WireframeDrawList.surveyEdges`.
    `surveyEdgeNote` writes the list's note, `SURVEY EDGE 4.21 km`, with `FROM CAMERA` where there is
    no own ship (`rangeText`'s form).
  - _Not wired into a view._ No view draws a body's terrain yet. Its terrain pass, the store and the
    pool's `onFieldChange` feeding a `CoverageMask`, `litBodiesOf`'s `surveyCoverage` and the draw
    list's `surveyEdges` with heights from the resident bakes wait for the first view that draws it,
    R10.T10.e's hand-over or T11's wireframe; the list's note and the tripod's give-way
    (`keepClear`) are T12's, whose text lists the note. The edge hidden by nearer terrain needs that
    terrain's depth in the symbology's pass: T11's depth-only terrain in the wireframe; over the

- **Questions for "main" (R10.T10.c)** (none touches the server's contracts; each built to its
  lean).
  - _The edge over the image, and the note's points, for R10.T16 and T12_ (the batch review,
    2026-10-19; nothing passes survey edges to a view yet). The photorealistic overlay's depth
    holds only the occluder spheres and the hulls' faces, so before survey edges reach it the
    overlay needs the terrain's depth, or nearer ground will not hide the edge over the image (nor,
    since the review, lines behind a surveyed body's equatorial limb; deferred below); and the note,
    and whether it stands, must count only the edge points the operator can see: a CPU march
    against `heightAtM`, or the depth-tested result. Lean: R10.T16's, as it wires the edges to the
    views.
  - _The discard's rule._ Design note 12's "interpolated mask below one half" draws both surfaces,
    or neither, along a half-quad strip at each coarse cell's edge; as built, the fragment's cell at
    its centre vertex (above), the half only where a cell spans one quad or less. Lean: as built,
    Design note 12 amended to "discards fragments outside a surveyed coarse cell, read from the
    survey mask at the cell's centre vertex".
  - _The field's code byte and stages._ The `survey-mask` field's 4,228 B carry the cell code in
    the last word's spare byte, and the field binds to both stages, where decision-r10-t10b-r09-t2e
    §5 foresaw one. Lean: as built; T11's wireframe reads the same field and code.
- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule) (R10.T10.c)** (recorded, not ruled; each leaves the
  algorithm and the contracts as built).
  - _A hole while a rebake is due._ The GPU mask takes a block's cells at once and a patch's mask
    takes them at its rebake, so for a rebake's latency (a bake, 40 to 140 ms) a newly surveyed cell
    is discarded by both surfaces along the survey's advancing edge. The lever: the terrain's
    discard reading the GPU mask too, or the GPU mask taking a block's cells once its patches'
    rebakes land.
  - _Fins at every sixteenth line._ Patches three to five levels coarser than the field (cells of
    8, 4 or 2 quads) have no fin on a coarse cell's edge that lies off lines 16, 32 and 48; such
    patches are drawn from a distance at which a step of a kilometre subtends a pixel or so. The
    lever: a fin every eighth line (half again the fins' vertices), or a fin draw of its own.
  - _The reference surface's edge in `f32`._ The reference surface's cell comes from an `f32` hit on
    the analytic spheroid, a few tenths of a metre to a metre off at a body's radius, the terrain's
    from its patch's coordinates, exact: across that width a pixel may be drawn by both (the depth
    test picks one) or by neither (the surveyed side's foot strip shows below). Seen only with metre
    pixels at the edge. The lever: the reference surface's cell from patch-relative coordinates.
  - _The limb draw keeps no mask._ A mesh body's limb, the disc's second draw, is drawn whole, over
    any surveyed terrain at the limb. The lever: the same discard in `bodyDiscDraw.wgsl` for a mesh
    body's limb.
  - _A skirt seen edge-on_ is shaded under the datum's normal at |μ|, which is 0 exactly edge-on,
    where it reflects nothing: a line one pixel wide at most.
  - _The cache's slots._ The `survey-mask` field takes 4,228 B a lit slot: 158,936 B, 422 slots in
    64 MiB on the low setting, against Design note 15's rule of 430; 311,024 B, 1,286 slots in
    400 MB on the high one. T14.
  - _The mark sits at the ground's own depth_ (the batch review, 2026-10-19). Once the terrain's
    depth is in the symbology's pass, a tick towards the camera sinks into the nearer ground, and
    the line on the step's rim z-fights with the higher surface. The lever: the ticks' ends on the
    ground, or the occluders' slope push for the terrain. For T11's GPU smoke.
  - _Datum-deep skirts._ Every surveyed patch's foot strips hang from its ground to the datum on
    all four edges, under its neighbours' surfaces, in a shader that discards, so hidden fragments
    may be shaded before the depth test rejects them; the overdraw grows with the ground's height
    above the datum, unmeasured. The lever: R05's skirt depth where no survey edge meets the patch
    edge. T14.
  - _A surveyed body's occluder at its polar radius_ (the batch review's choice, above). Between
    its sphere of c less the margin and its equatorial limb, a band up to a − c deep at the
    equator (21 km on Earth, some 15 px at the limb seen from 400 km up at 1080p across 60°),
    lines behind the body
    (another body's graticule, an orbit, a hull) are not hidden by the sphere. In the wireframe the
    body's terrain, which T11 draws to depth wherever the list draws its edge, covers the band;
    over the image the overlay holds no terrain depth yet (the question above). The lever: the
    terrain's depth in the overlay, or an occluder of the spheroid's own shape.
- **Deviations in T10.d, as built** (2026-10-16; lane r10-shader, on `rendering-and-planets` at

  - _Files._ The task's: a new `view/terrain/classMap.ts` (`CLASS_MAP_LEVEL`,

    `displays/view/photorealFrame.ts`, `viewFrameDrawer.ts` and `ViewDisplay.tsx`. Beyond them:
    `displays/view/useInstruments.ts` (the instruments' frames); the data path's
    `crates/hyperion-surface/src/worker.rs` (`WorkerFields::class_map`, `ClassMap`,
    `ClassMapClass`, `ClassMapTexel`, `CLASS_MAP_LEVEL`, `CLASS_MAP_BAND`, `CLASS_MAP_CLASSES`) with
    five tests in `worker/tests.rs`, `src/wasm.rs` (the `classMap` export, `ClassMapAnswer`, the
    shared `photometry_values`), and the client's `workers/messages.ts` (`ClassMapAnswer`, the
    `class-map` request, the `class-map` and `class-map-failed` replies, `classMapTransferables`),
    `workers/heightBake.ts` (`WasmClassMap`, `WorkerFields.classMap`, its answer) and
    `workers/pool.ts` (`HeightWorkerPool.classMap`); `test/scriptedHeightWorker.ts`
    (`pendingClassMaps`; its field messages by their kinds); the smoke harness's `smoke/bodies.ts`,
    and `smoke/litTerrain.ts` and `smoke/surveyEdge.ts`, whose replies' switches take the new kinds.
    No wire format, payload or golden changes: the worker query is a client message alone.
  - _The map's level_ (main's provisional ruling on R10.T2's question, confirmed against Design
    note 8). Quadtree level 6, band level 0: 64 texels along a face's side, each the cell
    (f, 6, i, j), its weights `weights_at` at band level 0. It is inside the ruling's bound (a map
    at L reads band level L − 6, Design note 8's "level 4 or shallower" bounding L at 10), and it is
    the only level that keeps Design note 8's "a few hundred kilobytes": with the gutter 66 × 66
    texels a layer, 104,544 B at four classes or fewer and 418,176 B at sixteen (24 layers), where a
    map at L = 10 would take about 100 MB. `weights_at` evaluates there from what the worker holds:
    a surveyed cell's centre reads its margin's cells (tested on the Moon-like field, level 6, and
    the Mars-like, level 7). The level is a named constant on both sides (`CLASS_MAP_LEVEL`).
  - _The data path_ (the lane lead's decision). An additive worker query,
    `HeightWorkerPool.classMap(body, detailSeed)`, a `Promise` answered by one worker, the least
    loaded, after the blocks posted before it, with the module's `classMap(system, body, seed)`:
    the classes (two bytes each, ≤ 16), their photometry (T10.b's five values a class: c `A_N` in
    B, V and R, the law's code, L(0)), and each texel the survey touches, by its cell index at
    level 6, with its surveyed share and its weight bytes; `null` where no payload field is held (a
    stand-in's included); a module refusal rejects with its message; a failed worker's query is
    asked again of its replacement after the fields, or of another worker, and of none answers
    `null`, as a terminated pool does.
  - _Partly surveyed texels_ (the lane lead's decision, as built). A texel's surveyed share is its
    field cells surveyed over its cells (4^(level − 6), margin cells unsurveyed), 1 where the field
    is at level 6 or shallower. Its weights are `weights_at` at its centre where the field cell
    holding the centre is surveyed, and otherwise the mean of `weights_at` at its surveyed cells'
    centres, both at band level 0, as bytes summing to 255 by the largest remainder; the client
    multiplies them by the share, so `elsewhere` takes the rest. A texel whose reads lack a cell is
    left out and the map marked incomplete (the store asks again at a block that brings cells).
  - _The classes._ Every material the texels name, in `GroundMaterial`'s order; past 16, the
    heaviest by weight × share summed over the texels (ties to the earlier material), the rest's
    weight left to `elsewhere`, not spread over the kept classes (asked below).
  - _Laws_ (the lane lead's decision). One per class, a full `PhotometricLaw` of its own:
    `{ ...classRowLaw(code, L(0)), a: c A_N }` from the worker's photometry, so the disc and the
    terrain take one row law each (identity-keyed rows hold: the store builds the laws once a map).
    A class whose palette names no substance (law code 0) shades with `elsewhere`, as the lit
    terrain's law 0 takes such a slot, so that its texel still counts as surveyed in the
    reconstruction. `elsewhere` is the body's photometry's law, given each frame
    (`ClassMapSource.classMapOf(body, elsewhere)`). R07's disc keeps `oblateAlbedoScale` on every
    law, the classes' included, as R07 built it; T10.e decides the terrain's side (T10.b's
    deferred "The class laws carry no figure scale").
  - _The gutter_ (the lane lead's decision): (N + 2) × (N + 2) texels a layer, face texel (i, j) at
    (i + 1, j + 1); each side of the gutter the edge texels of the neighbouring face across that
    edge (found by a point 10⁻⁹ past the edge, tested against R05's `edgeNeighbour`), its corners
    empty; the shader's N is `textureDimensions − 2`. This changes R07's recorded N × N layout
    (a pointer in R07's "Deviations in T8.b, as built"). R07's one-texel `bodies:no class map` stays,
    never read.
  - _The reconstruction_ (`surface_shares`, its twin `classMapSharesAt`): with n s and n t the
    point's place in texels, `elsewhere` alone where the texel holding it, (⌊n s⌋, ⌊n t⌋), holds no
    weight; otherwise each of the four texels from (⌊n s − ½⌋, ⌊n t − ½⌋), the gutter's at a face's
    edge, by its bilinear weight, those holding weight alone, each its own share vector
    (`surfaceShares`: `elsewhere`'s 1 − Σ w and the classes'), summed and renormalised. The texel
    holding the point is always one of the four at a bilinear weight of at least ¼. A partly
    surveyed texel counts as surveyed. `classWeightsAt` now reads a texel's own weights through the
    gutter's layout.
  - _The live store_ (the lane lead's decision). `ClassMapStore(engine, pool)`: `want(body,
detailSeed)` asks the pool, and it asks again after each of the body's blocks the workers take
    (the pool's `onFieldChange`, which follows the workers' coverage as T10.c's mask does) that
    surveys a cell, starts the field afresh, or brings a cell while the map is incomplete or
    absent; one query out a body, a change meanwhile asking again after it; an answer for a body
    released or asked for with another seed meanwhile dropped. It owns each texture (`<name>
    <body>`, `coarse-field-gpu`), remakes it at `onRestored` (a map answered during a loss waits
    for the restore), releases it with the body and at `dispose`, and reports a refused query once
    a body. Plumbing: `litBodiesOf(scene, pose, discs, classMaps?)` sets each body's `surface` from
    `classMaps.classMapOf(id, photometry.law)`, `PhotorealInputs.classMaps`,
    `ViewFrameInputs.classMaps`, `InstrumentsFrame.classMaps` and `ViewStage`'s `classMaps` prop,

    at its drawn time, none where it is `null`, whose class map then shades with `elsewhere`.

    hand-over range and back (the exposure locked at EV100 15.1 and 13.5), the disc 190 to 280 px
    across on high (on low larger, its range shorter, and in part under the label block), the 30°
    disc's gibbous face and the 90° disc's lit half evenly shaded to the terminator, with no block,
    seam, dark or bright texel at the survey; every read-back of the scene target was finite. What
    could not be judged: the reconstruction itself, since the fixture's surveyed ground is one law
    equal to the disc's elsewhere (every named material resolving to
    A 0.20 on the Regolith row; T10.e's record), so a correct map and a uniform one look the same;
    the disc's brightness off the survey is no check of an area-weighted photometry
    (decision-r10-t16d-part1, finding (a)). It waits for a served world with a patterned survey
    (T15). The owner's UHD 620 look stays his: `just views-check --terrain --setting low` (shown).
  - _Generator version._ Untouched (22): presentation alone; no golden moved, the worker golden
    included (the map is tested natively and on the module without one).
  - _The batch review (2026-10-19)._ The class map joins the worker's order-independence test, and
    the incomplete map is tested (a texel whose margin is in a block not yet taken is left out,
    then held, the map a fresh worker's); band level 0 is pinned in the weights goldens (new lines
    at 22, no existing line moved; main's ruling on R10.T2's Q2); and the texel loop's allocations
    are hoisted. On the client, the tests that failed for more than one reason are split, one
    behaviour an `it` (`classMap.test.ts`' refusals and the store's restore, release, listener and
    disposal; `heightBake.test.ts`' and `pool.test.ts`' class-map queries).
- **Questions for "main" (R10.T10.d)** (none touches a contract of the server's; each built to its
  lean).
  - _Who wires the live store and pool._ No live view creates a `CoarseFieldStore` or a
    `HeightWorkerPool`, and no plan-10 task names wiring them. Lean: the task that first draws a
    body's terrain live (T10.e's hand-over, or T11's wireframe if it lands first) makes the store
    over the view's engine and the pool in `ViewStage`, beside T10.c's `CoverageMask`, and passes it
    as `classMaps`. _Answered 2026-10-16: R10.T16 "The live terrain path"
    (decision-r10-live-path.md)._
  - _The map's level in the text._ Lean: Design note 8's "T2's weights at level 4 or shallower"
    and T2's "the class map's level (level 4)" read "a texel a cell of quadtree level 6, its
    weights at band level 0" (main's provisional ruling, confirmed here).
  - _Past sixteen classes._ Lean: as built, the lightest classes' weight left to `elsewhere`; the
    alternative, T2's spreading over the kept classes, would shade unknown ground with known laws.
  - _A class of no named substance_ shades with `elsewhere` and counts as surveyed. Lean: as built,
    as the lit terrain's law 0.
  - _The cell pass_ (Risks, "Class-map discs and R07's cell pass"): still open, for the
    orchestrator; T10.d keeps class-map discs out of it as R07 built.
- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule) (R10.T10.d)** (recorded, not ruled; each leaves the
  algorithm and the contracts as built).
  - _Band level 0's agreement is unmeasured._ T2 held the weights to counted classes at n − 1 to
    n − 6 and at band level 4; the map reads band level 0, a texel of 1/64 of a face's side, whose
    own agreement no test states. The lever: T2's slow agreement case at band level 0.
  - _A partly surveyed texel whose centre's cell is surveyed_ takes the centre's weights for its
    surveyed part, where the mean over its surveyed cells would weigh only them. The lever: always
    the mean (up to sixteen `weights_at` a texel at level 8).
  - _A whole map a block._ Each block that surveys cells asks for the whole map: 24,576 texels
    scanned and a `weights_at` (13 to 26 µs, T2's figures) for each surveyed texel, about 0.3 s on
    one worker for 10⁴ texels, beside its bakes. The lever: asking for the texels a block's cells
    touch alone.
  - _At a cube's corner_ three texels meet and the gutter's corner is empty, so within half a texel
    of a corner the reconstruction renormalises over three: continuous across each edge, not
    exactly at the corner.
  - _The centre's cell at field levels 7 and 8_ (the batch review's consider item, 2026-10-19).
    There a texel's centre is the corner where four of its 4 or 16 field cells meet, so which cell
    is "the centre's" is settled by `PatchKey::containing`'s rounding of the st → uv → xyz → st
    round trip: deterministic on every target, but an integer choice of the child,
    `(i << shift) + (side >> 1)`, would be exact.
- **Deviations in T10.e, as built** (2026-10-16; lane r10-shader, on `rendering-and-planets` at
  `05da4caf`).
  - _Files._ A new `view/terrain/handover.ts` (`pixelAngleRad`, `handoverRangeM`,
    `handoverReliefM`, `limbDistanceM`, `handoverTauPx`, `handsOver`, `handoverRangeRatio`,
    `HandoverSphere`, `handOverRegimes`, `HandoverReliefSource`, `storeReliefSource`) with
    `handover.test.ts` and `handover.wasm.test.ts`; `view/quality/qualitySetting.ts`
    (`WIREFRAME_TERRAIN_TAU_PX`); R07's `bodies/regime.ts` (`LitRegime`'s `terrain`, `drawnAsMesh`,
    the promotion's writers), `bodies/draw.ts` (`LitBodyInput.handoverReliefM`,
    `MeshBodyPlan.handedOver`, `planLitBodies`' hand-over, the coverage mask's reader),
    `bodies/discShading.ts` (`discReflectance`, `scaledLawOf`) and `photoreal/renderer.ts`
    (`FrameTerrain`, `PhotorealFrame.terrain`, its draws in the `bodies` pass);
    `displays/view/photorealFrame.ts` (`PhotorealInputs.reliefs` and `terrain`,
    `LitBodiesTerrain`, `litBodiesOf`'s fifth argument) and `viewFrameDrawer.ts`
    (`ViewFrameInputs.reliefs` and `terrain`); `view/terrain/terrainMaterial.ts` (`figureScaledA`,
    `packClassLaws`' and `classTexelLaw`'s c ÷ a, `terrainTexelLaws`), `gpu/resources.ts` (passes
    the figure's c ÷ a), `shaders/terrainLit.wgsl` (a comment alone) and `coarseFieldStore.ts`
    (`FieldCandidate.rangeRatio`'s documentation); the smoke harness's `smoke/surveyEdge.ts`, whose
    reference body is now handed over. Tests beside them in `terrainMaterial.test.ts`,
    `draw.test.ts`, `regime.test.ts`, `renderer.test.ts` and `photorealFrame.test.ts`.
  - _The range, pure_ (the lane lead's decision). `handoverRangeM(reliefM, tauPx, radPerPx)` is
    relief ÷ (τ · rad a pixel), refusing a relief negative or not finite and a τ or pixel not
    positive: at Design note 13's 5.454 × 10⁻⁴ rad a pixel, 1.833 × 10⁷ m for 10 km at 1 px and
    4.584 × 10⁶ m at 4 px (the task's 1.8 × 10⁷ and 4.6 × 10⁶ m). The view passes R07's own pixel,
    `pixelAngleRad` = 2 tan(fov ÷ 2) ÷ width, the inverse of `angularDiameterPx`'s centre-pixel
    scale that `litRegimes` measures its 3 px switch by, so that both switches count pixels alike:
    6.014 × 10⁻⁴ rad at 1080p across 60°, where 10 km hands over at 1.663 × 10⁷ m (4.157 × 10⁶ m at
    4 px), as R07's orchestrator ruling of 2026-10-03 took the centre pixel for its own figures.
  - _The distance is the limb's_ (beyond the decisions; asked below). `handsOver` sets the range
    against the camera's distance to the body's limb, √(D² − a²) for a camera D from the centre of
    a body of equatorial radius a (`limbDistanceM`, 0 from inside), not the centre's: there the
    relief stands against the sky across the line of sight. Far off the two agree (the centre is
    7% farther at an Earth's 1.663 × 10⁷ m, which a live 1080p view so reaches from 1.781 × 10⁷ m
    off its centre); near the ground the limb's goes to 0, so a body whose relief is small beside
    its radius still hands over as the camera nears it. From the centre it would not: a Venus of
    6,051.8 km and 13 km of relief has a wireframe range of 5.40 × 10⁶ m, inside its radius, and
    would never hand over there, landed or not; from its limb it hands over some 1,740 km up
    (`handover.test.ts`). `handoverRangeRatio(limbM, reliefM, tauPx, radPerPx)` gives
    `FieldCandidate.rangeRatio` by the same distance, `Infinity` with no relief (R10.T7's lean),
    and that field's documentation now says so (T7 computed none), so that a body's field is wanted
    before it hands over.
  - _τ per style_ (the lane lead's decision). `handoverTauPx(style, setting)`: the settings'
    `TerrainSettings.tauPx` in the photorealistic style (1 px high, 2 px low) and
    `WIREFRAME_TERRAIN_TAU_PX` = 4 in the wireframe on both settings, a named constant beside
    `TERRAIN_SETTINGS`.
  - _The relief_ (the lane lead's decision). `handoverReliefM(header, coverage)` is the header's
    `realised_relief_m`, as Design note 13 names R09's `realised_relief`, where a header and a
    coverage whose `surveyedFraction()` is above 0 are held, and `null` otherwise (and for a relief
    of 0 or not finite): `null` never hands over, at any distance. `storeReliefSource(store)` reads
    a `CoarseFieldStore`'s `header` and `coverage` through it. Design note 13's one-sided example is
    a deferred finding below.
  - _The hysteresis applies naturally, and is R07's_ (the lane lead's decision). `handsOver` takes
    `REGIME_HYSTERESIS` on the relief's subtense as R07's switch takes it on the diameter: a body
    hands over once its relief subtends τ (1 + h) px at its limb, the limb within range ÷ 1.1, and
    hands back once under τ (1 − h), past range ÷ 0.9. The previous frame's state is the regime
    map's own `terrain`, which the views already carry (`previousRegimes`); `litRegimes` keeps a
    `terrain` body on the disc side of its 3 px switch as it keeps a `mesh`.
  - _The decision, per view and style_ (the lane lead's decision). `LitRegime` gains `terrain`, the
    mesh regime whose ground R05's quadtree draws (Design note 13: "the `mesh` regime hands its
    geometry to R05's quadtree"), a fourth value rather than `mesh` with a flag, so that the
    hysteresis reads the previous frame from the map R07 already passes and a mesh by promotion
    is not taken for one handed over (asked below). `planLitBodies` runs `litRegimes`, then
    `handOverRegimes` (each disc with a relief, at the photorealistic style's τ on
    `options.setting` and `pixelAngleRad` of the frame's camera and viewport, the pixel the 3 px
    switch measures), then `promoteOverlapping`, whose writers now include a body handed over
    (`drawnAsMesh`), so that a disc overlapping it is promoted. A point never hands over: its flux
    is the point regime's, T10.f's. A body handed over is drawn as a mesh body is (its smooth figure
    in the `bodies` pass, its limb in the sequence), its `MeshBodyPlan.handedOver` set, its figure
    the reference surface beneath its terrain: T10.c's coverage mask is now read for a body handed
    over alone, so that a body promoted by its overlaps draws its figure whole (T10.c read any
    mesh body's; no view gave one). The terrain input is `PhotorealFrame.terrain?: FrameTerrain`,
    the view's: `surveyCoverage(body)`, which `litBodiesOf` passes as each body's
    `surveyCoverage`, and `draws(plan)`, drawn in the `bodies` pass after the figures; the reliefs
    are `PhotorealInputs.reliefs` (a `HandoverReliefSource`), which `litBodiesOf` passes as each
    body's `handoverReliefM`. `ViewFrameInputs` takes both, optional. Without a terrain input a body
    handed over is drawn as a mesh body is, its figure whole; without reliefs none hands over.
  - _Not built_ (the lane lead's decision; asked below). The live pipeline: no view makes a
    `CoarseFieldStore` over `surface_field`, a `HeightWorkerPool`, a `TerrainPass` per view and

    its τ is built and tested (`handoverTauPx("wireframe", …)`, `handsOver` at 4 px), its draw is
    T11's.
  - _One row, one figure scale_ (the lane lead's decision). The terrain's class laws now take the
    body's figure scale as the disc's laws do (`scaledLaws`): each class's A is c A_N times
    `oblateAlbedoScale` of its L(0) and the body's c ÷ a (`figureScaledA`, in `packClassLaws`, which
    `TerrainResources.upload` calls with its figure's c ÷ a, and in the twins `classTexelLaw` and
    `terrainTexelLaws`, the latter the twin of `packTerrainLighting`'s law 0 and `packClassLaws`'
    slots), retiring T10.b's deferred "The class laws carry no figure scale". The factor is 1 under
    Lommel–Seeliger's L(0) = 1, whose disc reaches p on any figure, 1.0062 for the Ice row at
    L(0) 0.628 and 1.0224 under Lambert's at c ÷ a 0.9, and 1 + 2.4 × 10⁻⁴ under Lambert's on the
    Moon-like world (c ÷ a 0.9988; the code's 1 + 2.85 × 10⁻⁴ carries R07's quadrature bias,
    deferred below). It is right as the disc's is: T10.a's c is solved on the
    sphere's p, and the factor takes the disc to that p equator-on, so the terrain under it draws
    the disc's light a class. T10.b's tests are unchanged but for the new argument (1, a sphere).
    `discShading.ts` exports `discReflectance(laws, c ÷ a, shares, μ₀, μ, α)`, the disc's own
    `surfaceReflectance` at h = μ₀ with no source radius, through the same scaling.
  - _The agreement_ (`handover.test.ts`). Per class law, Regolith (A 0.172, 0.142, 0.105 in r, g,

  - _The residuals of T10.a against plan 14's p and q._ p: T10.a's own record ("Deviations in
    T10.a, as built", the table): in V zero to rounding (at most 2 × 10⁻¹⁶ relative) on every
    served world, in B and R +35% and −17% on Mercury's colour and +93% and −41% on Mars's, the grey
    palettes'. q, computed now (`handover.test.ts`): a patterned sphere's orientation-averaged phase
    integral is Σ aᵢ pᵢ qᵢ ÷ Σ aᵢ pᵢ, as its p is the area average (T10.a's module documentation),
    so on a world whose ground takes one class law it is that law's whatever the albedos. The
    airless worlds of T10.a's table (the Moon- and Ceres-like and the reference Moon and Ceres, all
    regolith or bedrock of silicate families, the Regolith row by `PhaseLaw::for_family`) and the
    reference Mars's dust take the Regolith row, q 0.62600 under McEwen's L(α) (V), against plan
    14's 0.47980 on Mercury's template (+30.5%) and 1.08465 on Mars's at L 0.5 (−42.3%) (deferred
    below). The Mars-like world, whose glaciers take Lambert's row (q 3/2) on 1.5% of its area at
    their clamped albedos, waits on T10.f's point integral or those albedos; the Earth-like is not
    served a scale.

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule) (R10.T10.f)** (recorded, not ruled; each leaves the
  algorithm and the contracts as built).
  - _The eclipse's limb weighting is the uniform law's._ Under a patterned map each star's
    `discEclipseVisible` weights the disc by `elsewhere`'s L, not by the classes' A and L where the
    shadow falls. The error is first order in partial phases (the batch review's science check,
    2026-10-19): the product of the pattern's contrast and the eclipse's variation across the disc;
    a sharp shadow over exactly the bright half of a 14:1 body gives the point 7.5 times its light,
    over the dark half 0.54 times. The lever stays a per-element eclipse in the integral, which
    would be exact (the cache then holding the uncut ratio and the eclipse its own factor).
  - _R07's disc at 3 px misses a pattern's edge near the limb._ R07.T8.c's 8 × 8 cells integrate
    the two cells nearest the limb across their profile in √δ, as a uniform law's light needs; the
    Iapetus's bright rim, 0.06 a inside the limb facing the leading side, lies in that band, and its
    albedo step is not followed: the disc is 1.73%, 1.99% and 2.58% under the point facing the
    leading side at 0°, 60° and 120°, and 1.73% facing a pole at 120° (the point within 2 × 10⁻⁴
    of the brute force there; 4.1% at 150°, measured with one element a texel). At 32 × 32 it is
    still 1.1% to 1.7% off, the band about the rim's width; at 64 × 64 the band lies inside it. So
    the 3 px switch steps by up to 0.03 mag for such a body. The lever: R07.T8.c's limb cells
    under a class map (more of them, or each Gauss depth of the profile taking its own shares).
  - _Planetshine from a class-mapped neighbour_ keeps the neighbour's photometry law
    (`litNeighbours` through `bodyReflection`), so a patterned moon lights its planet by its mean,
    not by the face it turns to it. The lever: the neighbour's light through
    `classMapPointReflection` towards the lit body.
  - _A map's first point costs a frame._ The elements' shares, 98,304 `classMapSharesAt` calls,
    take about 300 ms on the render thread the first time a point is drawn under each map the store
    takes, and each light's evaluation 1.65 ms; under time acceleration a fast rotator misses the
    cache every frame (δ at α = 0 is 10⁻³ rad, which an Earth-like day turns through in 14 s of
    game time). The levers: the shares built off the frame (with the map in the worker, or as the
    store takes it), a reconstruction loop cheaper than `classMapSharesAt`'s allocations, and
    uniform texels' elements merged.
  - _Memory._ The elements' geometry, 3.1 MB once, and each map's shares 1–2 MB, against its
    texture's 104–418 KB. The lever: directions found per face from tabulated (u, v), or `f32`
    stores.
  - _T10.e's q for the Mars-like world is not closed by the point integral_ (T10.e's deferred "The
    classes' q is the Regolith row's, not plan 14's"). The integral is linear in the map, so
    averaged over orientations it gives T10.e's closed form Σ aᵢ pᵢ qᵢ ÷ Σ aᵢ pᵢ exactly and adds
    nothing to it, and no client fixture holds the Mars-like world's class map (its field is the
    surface crate's synthetic world; the worker golden is the Moon-like's). By the closed form, from
    T10.a's `albedo/worlds.golden` (dust 98.29%, two glaciers 0.770% each, sediment 0.166%,
    p_V 0.17) with the glaciers clamped low (T10.a's table) to their spans' low ends under Lambert's
    law, the H₂O glacier's `GLACIER_ICE_V` 0.69 and, taking CO₂ as a volatile ice,
    `VOLATILE_GLACIER_V`'s 0.80 (p 0.460 and 0.533), and the dust and sediment on the Regolith row
    (q 0.62600 in V) taking the rest of p: q_V ≈ 0.665, the glaciers 4.5% of p, against plan 14's
    1.08465 on Mars's template (−38.7%). Not checked against the worker's photometry export; T10.e's
    finding stands, for plan 14 and R10.T1.a's rows.
- **Deviations in T16.a, as built** (2026-10-19; lane r10-live, on `rendering-and-planets` at
  `b021342b`).

  - _The session's surface_ (the lane lead's decision 1, as suggested but where stated).
    `new TerrainSession({ engine, universe, requests, linkUp, createWorker, workers? })`, with
    `workers` Design note 11's default of `navigator.hardwareConcurrency` where absent;
    `noteView(id, report)`, `forgetView(id)`, `step()`, `setLinkUp`, `noteSurfaceRevisions`,
    `resync()`; the getters `classMaps` (the `ClassMapStore`) and `reliefs`
    (`storeReliefSource` over the store); `survey(body)`, a `TerrainSurvey` (the store's
    `FieldStatus`, coverage and header, `stale` the coverage's or, with none, the link's down),
    `null` for a body not wanted; `coverageMask(body)`, the mask's texture or `null`; `memory()`;
    `dispose()`. Added: `wanted`, `workerCount` and `detailSeed(body)` (T16.b's pass source takes
    the seed). Every method but the getters does nothing once disposed, since a view's loop may run
    a frame on a session its source has just let go.
    - _`step()` takes no time._ The suggested `step(nowMs)` would leave its argument unused, which
      the lint refuses. _(Corrected by F2, the batch review's C8: T16.b did not add it either; each
      view's debounce takes its own draw's time, `TerrainViewFrameInput.nowMs`.)_
  - _The pool before lanes_ (decision 2). `HeightWorkerPoolOptions.bake` is optional; a pool
    without it holds fields and answers class maps, and its `request`, `reprioritise` and
    `cancelStale` throw ("made without bake settings"). Every spike and pool test passes unchanged;
    `pool.test.ts` gains the session pool's (refusals, fields, `keptFieldBytes`, the count).
  - _The worker count_ (decision 3). `defaultHeightWorkers` in `workers/pool.ts`;
    `defaultSpikeWorkers` delegates to it under its old name, so `displays/` imports nothing of
    `view/spike/`. A count the browser does not give as a finite number takes one worker (an added
    guard: ⌊NaN ÷ 4⌋ clamps to NaN, which the pool refuses).
  - _`ViewStage`'s prop_ (decision 4). `terrain: TerrainSession | null` replaces `classMaps`; the
    loop reads the session through its inputs' ref, steps it once each frame the primary draws,
    before the draw (whether or not a drawer is made, so that a device loss releases nothing), and
    gives its `classMaps` and `reliefs` to the primary's `ViewFrameInputs` and the
    `InstrumentsFrame`. Each view reports after a frame it drew (`terrainReportOf`, `null` while its
    stage is not laid out), and has the session forget it when the session changes, its loop ends,
    or (an instrument) it closes or its canvas goes. The instruments draw in the primary's frame
    after it, so their reports reach the next step. `ViewFrameDrawer.regimes` exposes `#regimes`:
    the last photorealistic plan's, which a frame drawn in the wireframe leaves as they were (T16.b
    reads them with the report's `style`).
  - _The candidates_ (decision 5), `viewFieldCandidates(report, reliefM)`, pure. `local` is the
    camera's frame (`sceneFrameFor` over `cameraSceneOf(scene)`); the distance is the body's drawn
    centre from the camera (`relativeToCamera` of the body frame's origin), the limb's at
    `ViewBody.radiusM` (the figure's a where plan 14 sends a figure); `reliefM` the held header's
    `realised_relief_m`, `Infinity` without one. The report's `style` is the budget's (the style the
    view is to draw), so a photorealistic view whose pipelines still compile is judged at 1 px.
    The pixel is the presented width's centre pixel (`pixelAngleRad` of the canvas's device px,
    decision 5), where T10.e's hand-over measures the frame's internal viewport (asked below).
  - _The sources_ (decision 6). `terrainSessionSource(stage)` is pure: the server's scene of the
    open universe over `useServerLink()`'s request client, a kept scene's `SceneOption.terrain`, and
    `null` otherwise (every kept scene today). A `TerrainFixture` is `{ universe, open() }`, its link
    `{ requests, onSurface, close }`, always up, opened once a session and closed after it; T16.d
    fills it for `TERRAIN TEST`, and the hook's test holds the seam with a test-only option over a
    `RequestClient` of its own. `ViewBody.detailSeed` is optional. The hook makes the session in an
    effect (keyed by the engine, the universe and request client or the fixture, the worker factory
    and count) and holds it in a `useSyncExternalStore` holder rather than state, takes the link's
    state through a ref when it makes one and an effect after, and subscribes the scene's
    `onSurface` (or the fixture's) in an effect of its own. A `ViewStage` remounted on a new scene
    of the same source keeps the session (the hook is in `ViewPanels`).
  - _The worker factory_ (beyond the decisions). `ViewDisplayProps.heightWorkers` starts a height
    worker, `browserHeightWorker` (the module worker on `view/terrain/workers/height.worker.ts`) by
    default. jsdom has no `Worker`, and a server scene now makes a session in every display test, so
    the shared harness and `ViewDisplay.test.tsx` pass scripted workers
    (`ViewDisplayHarness.heightWorkers` lists them). `App.tsx` passes none.
  - _The masks forget with the workers_ (beyond the decisions). The store posts through a
    `FieldPool` the session gives it, whose `fieldRelease` makes the body's mask forget its cells
    first (`#fieldReleased`): a field released, refused by a worker, of another history (a refused
    `have_revision`), not modelled, or a first payload that failed. `CoverageMask` only adds cells
    (T10.c), so a dropped field's mask would otherwise keep discarding the reference surface where
    no field holds ground. T16.b disposes the body's passes at the same point (D4).
  - _The GPU mask's timing_ (decision 7). `#blockTaken(change)` is the masks' one feed from the
    workers, at once, as T10.c built it; T16.b gates it there.
  - _Memory_ (decision 8). `TerrainSessionMemory` is `workerFieldBytes` (`fieldResidentBytes`),
    `keptFieldBytes` (the pool's new getter: every kept field's blocks) and `gpuBytes`, by category.
    The GPU bytes are the session's own handles, made through a wrapper of the engine that holds
    each texture's bytes by the engine's own rule (`textureBytes`), not the engine's allocation tally
    (`allocationTally`), which counts every allocation of a category whoever made it, from when the
    tally is made; `coarse-field-gpu` is the session's alone in `VIEW` today, so the two agree there.
    The masks and maps are under `coarse-field-gpu`, as built.
  - _Teardown_ (decision 9), in order: the passes (none yet; a comment marks the place), the
    class-map store, the session's listeners and the masks (each body's detail-seed request
    cancelled with its mask), the store (its requests and timers cancelled, `field-release` posted
    to every worker), then the pool (its workers terminated). Tested: no worker running or
    listening, the request and the retry timer gone, the `coarse-field-gpu` tally back to zero,
    nothing made at a restore after, and the class map released before the mask and the fields
    before the workers stop.
  - _The detail seed._ `bodyDetailSeed(record)` (`bodiesWire.ts`, sharing its form with
    `toBodyDetail`'s check) reads `hooks.detail_seed` alone: `null` where either section is not
    `ok` or the seed is malformed. One `body_detail` a want, at the time of the scene of the first
    report holding the body; a link lost meanwhile asks it again at the return; any other refusal,
    and hooks not `ok`, give no seed until the body is wanted afresh; a release cancels it. With
    the seed the session wants the body's class map, which T10.d's store asks once the workers hold
    the field. R08.T10.a's sharing has its one place (`#askSeed`).
  - _The scene's revisions_ (G4). `SceneUpdate`'s `ok` carries the push's `surfaceRevisions`, in the
    order sent, none for a push that names none, and the model keeps none (applying a push with
    them gives the model the push without them gives). A `surface_revisions` that is not a list of
    bodies with whole revisions of at least 1 is a fault, `surface revisions unusable`, after which
    `useScene` resubscribes as for any unusable push. `useScene`'s `SceneView.onSurface(listener)`
    hands `SceneSurfaceEvent`s (`revisions`, or `resync` when a subscription opened by a
    resubscription is adopted, the link up throughout) to listeners, never to the snapshot, so that
    a push naming revisions renders as one that names none; a link return's opening tells no
    resync, since the link's own state asks the fields again. A listener that throws is reported
    and leaves the scene and the others as they were.
  - _The store's resync_ (the task's "where a seam needs it"). `CoarseFieldStore.resync()` asks
    every kept field again with the revision held, as the link's return does; one whose request is
    in flight is asked again once it is answered (its answer may predate the rise), and one held
    failed or not modelled is not asked.

- **Questions for "main" (R10.T16.a)** (none touches a contract of the server's; each built to its
  lean). _Main's ruling: none relayed to the lane by F2 (2026-10-20); the lane lead marks each
  here as main rules it._
  - _The want's pixel._ The field's want is judged at the presented width's centre pixel (decision
    5), where T10.e's hand-over takes the frame's internal viewport (T10.e's deferred "The
    hand-over moves with the frame's internal scale"), so at a scale of 0.5 the want's range is
    twice the hand-over's and a body's field is fetched as early as at full scale. Lean: as built;
    T10.e's lever (both switches on the presented pixel) would make them one. _Ruled
    (decision-r10-t16-leans §13): accepted; R10.T10.g takes T10.e's lever, both switches on the
    presented pixel._
  - _A header with no surveyed ground._ The want takes the header's relief whatever the coverage, so
    a field whose survey covers nothing is kept within its range, though `handoverReliefM` gives
    such a body no hand-over. Lean: as built (the want follows the relief alone, so that the first
    survey's cells reach a field already held). _Ruled (decision-r10-t16-leans §13): accepted._
  - _The session's GPU bytes._ Counted from its own handles, not the engine's tally (above). Lean:
    as built; R12's memory line reads the engine's tally by category and the session's report beside
    it. _Ruled (decision-r10-t16-leans §13): accepted, recorded in R12's Consumes._
- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule) (R10.T16.a)** (recorded, not ruled; each leaves the
  algorithm and the contracts as built).
  - _Workers start with the session._ Its pool's workers are started, and each loads the surface
    module, when the session is made, before any body is wanted: every show of `VIEW` on a server
    scene starts them, whether or not a camera nears a body. Unmeasured; T14 states it with the
    re-show's fetches. The lever: a pool made at the first want.
  - _The candidates each primary frame._ Each step remakes every view's camera scene
    (`cameraSceneOf`) and frame (`sceneFrameFor`) and every lit body's distance, up to three views'
    worth: small beside a frame, unmeasured. The lever: the drawer's own camera scene handed with
    the report.
  - _The seed's time._ A body's `body_detail` is asked at its scene's time; one absent from its
    record then (`hooks` `not_applicable`) has no seed until it is wanted afresh, though its field
    may be held. The scene's bodies are present at its time, so this is a server's edge case.
  - _Display tests now make sessions._ Every display test on a server scene makes a session with
    scripted workers, and asks `surface_field` and `body_detail` where the camera is in a lit body's
    frame; no existing test reads them, and all pass unchanged.
- **Ruled for T16** (`decision-r10-t16-contracts.md`, 2026-10-19; the lane's seven questions). Q1
  (the engine's releases) and Q7 (the fault, on the label block's fault lines) differ from the
  lane's leans; Q2–Q6 take them with conditions. Folded into T16.b–d's text above, plan 05's
  Design note 9 and plan 01's "Extended by" list. Its deferred findings (recorded, not ruled):
  - _R01-1: other per-view objects keep their meshes and materials._ Objects disposed while the
    engine lives still leave their small meshes and materials, once an instrument's lifetime:
    `PhotorealRenderer`'s sprite quad and triangle, the wireframe's, the bodies', the sky's and the
    bloom chain's. Their owners adopt `releaseMesh` and `releaseMaterial` when they next touch them.
  - _R01-2 (T14): a hand-over's churn._ Each hand-over compiles the terrain material afresh and
    allocates a whole cache budget of 64–400 MB, so a pass made and dropped at an instrument's zoom
    churns both. T14 measures it beside "The live path's costs" and decides whether passes share a
    material or a cache, and whether the field's release hysteresis takes a view's field of view.
  - _For the sensors plan and R11: a craft's site off the survey._ Until the craft's own sensors
    survey it, the picture shows the reference surface under a craft standing at its true height
    (the server's `ground_at` over the whole field), above or below it by the local relief.
  - _For T14.c: the contact's height and ground point._ T16.b's contact rule measures "under 1 km
    over the datum" and passes the datum's point, behind one function; over surveyed relief the
    datum can be kilometres off, so a craft landing on a plateau would never count as descending.
    T14.c gives that function the workers' ground, amends Design note 9's "above the spheroid" to
    "above the ground where it is held", tests a landing on a plateau more than 1 km above the
    datum, and takes the level table's highest bound for the ground track's floors off the survey.
    _Ruled (decision-r10-t14c-leans §4): "the level table's highest bound" off the survey is the
    body-wide ceiling, the table's highest over its rows plus the header's realised relief and a
    metre (`reading.rs`' `ceiling_m`); the workers' table alone bounds only the cells held._
  - _The two discards on hardware._ The terrain discards by a mask interpolated over its vertices,
    the reference surface by one sampled from a texture; they may differ by part of a pixel at the
    edge on hardware where SwiftShader agrees. Left to the by-hand look at T10.c's edge, on the
    RTX 3080 (hidden) and the owner's UHD 620.
  - _For R07.T20's owner (pre-existing)._ `viewsCheck.sh` uses `setsid` and GNU `timeout`, which
    macOS lacks and Windows has only under a POSIX shell; the terrain flag adds nothing new.
  - _For R02: `KEPT_SYSTEM` is a canonical layer-A ID_ (`SystemId::from_parts`' doc example), so a
    kept scene's bodies could share an ID with a real galaxy's system; harmless while kept scenes
    never reach the server.
  - _The `GRAPHICS` panel_ lists `GRAPHICS VIEW REFUSED` beside the label block; whether it lists
    the terrain fault too is R12's settings ladder's, or the next plan's to touch the panel.
  - _For T12:_ with every worker lost, the readings cannot be made (lean: Missing, the em dash, the
    fault line standing as the cause); the survey line's state for a refused field is T12's, its
    T16.d draft going to the sign-off queue.
- **Deviations in T16.b, as built** (2026-10-19; lane r10-live, on `rendering-and-planets` at
  `b021342b`, after T16.a's `63e31fe4`).
  - _Files._ New: `view/terrain/surveyLookup.ts` (`SurveyedCells`) with `surveyLookup.test.ts` and
    `surveyLookup.wasm.test.ts`; `view/terrain/terrainPassShared.test.ts`;
    `view/terrain/sessionPasses.test.ts` (joins `vitest.config.mts`' `DOM_TESTS`);
    `displays/view/viewFaults.ts` (`faultFor`, moved out of `ViewDisplay.tsx`, and `faultsFor`)
    with its test; `smoke/sharedPass.ts`. Changed: the task's `workers/pool.ts`, `terrainPass.ts`,
    `select.ts`, `cache.ts`, `grounded.ts`, `session.ts`; R01's `view/engine/{types,resilientEngine}.ts`,
    `webgpu/{engine,meshes}.ts`, `test/{fakeRenderEngine,countingRenderEngine}.ts`,
    `displays/view/check/probedEngine.ts`; `displays/view/ViewLabelBlock.tsx`, `InstrumentView.tsx`
    and `ViewDisplay.tsx`; beyond them `gpu/resources.ts`, `workers/rebake.ts` (`RebakeLayers`),
    `annunciation.ts` (`TERRAIN_NOT_AVAILABLE`), `terrainMaterial.ts`,
    `displays/view/useTerrainSession.ts` (`useTerrainFaults`), `view/spike/DescentSpike.tsx` (its
    fault as a list), `test/terrainFixtures.ts`, `smoke/page.ts`, and tests beside each.
    `view/spike/spikeRun.ts` is unchanged: `TerrainPoolFactory` keeps its type, and the session's
    factory gives a lane. No wire format, payload, shader, Rust code or golden changes.
  - _The releases_ (decision-r10-t16-contracts §1), as plan 01's "Extended by R10.T16.b" has them.
    `MeshRecord` keeps its buffers' handles (`buffers`), which `releaseMesh` destroys; a released
    mesh or material is refused as "was released" by a draw, by `createMaterialAsync`'s `meshes`
    and by a second release. `ResilientEngine` notes the maker of meshes and materials too (an
    asynchronous material's maker is the engine asked). `FakeRenderEngine` now makes mesh and
    material handles and records their releases. `CountingRenderEngine` gains `live` (the handles
    of each kind made and not released) and `loseHandles()`, which models a loss's end of every
    handle (each buffer's and texture's `destroyed` event, a later release dropped as
    `ResilientEngine` drops it); its meshes still raise no allocation events. `TerrainResources`
    releases every handle it made at `dispose`, the mesh and every view's buffers included, and at
    a restore releases the lost device's first (dropped by `ResilientEngine`), so that a counting
    engine restored without `loseHandles` leaves none either.
  - _The pool's lanes._ `HeightWorkerPool.lane(bake)` returns a `HeightWorkerLane`, an interface
    the pool fills (not a class, so that no internal type reaches a public signature):
    `settings`, `currentGeneration`, `queuedCount`, `waitingCount`, `unavailable`
    (`lostWorkers === workerCount`), `terminated`, `request`, `reprioritise`, `cancelStale`,
    `onBaked`, `onFailed` and `terminate`. A pool made with `bake` holds its own lane, which its own
    calls reach, so the spike's pool and its tests are unchanged; `queuedCount` and `waitingCount`
    now sum the lanes. Added: `workerCount`, and `fieldBlocks(body)` (the blocks posted and
    reported of the field's current start), which the session's coverage gate reads. An answer to
    a terminated lane's request is dropped as it arrives, its record still counting against the
    worker's two in flight.
  - _The shared pass._ `TerrainPass.step({ views, grounded })` selects once over the views that
    hand the body over (`TerrainPassView`: `id`, `view`, its style's `tauPx`, `weight`), and
    `drawFor(id, input)` gives one view's `TerrainViewFrame`: `draw`, `conditions`, the debounced
    `annunciation`, `fault`, `missing`, `standingIn` and `maskReady` (no fault, nothing it sees
    missing, and its draw made wherever it sees a patch: decision D7's rule, T16.c's to apply).
    `frame(input)` is a step and a draw of `DEFAULT_TERRAIN_VIEW` ("primary"), bit for bit R05's:
    every pass and spike test passes unchanged. Added: `forgetView`, `setLevels`, `fieldChanged`,
    and the getters `planet`, `settled`, `faulted`, `viewIds`, `lastStep` and `resident(key)`.
    `TerrainPool` gains the optional `onFailed` and `unavailable`; `HeightWorkerPool` has no
    `unavailable`, so the spike's pass keeps drawing what is resident with every worker lost, as
    built. A view left out of a step is forgotten at once, its buffers released; a view's records,
    bands, uniforms, draw and debounce are its own; `#due` selects again on a change of the views,
    any view's field of view, size, τ or weight, the level table or the survey's `version`, and on
    each view's own turn and move (its own nearest coarse patch, or `Selection.nearestSurveyM` with
    none). Each view's `DETAIL LIMITED` is `limited && limitExcess > w`, or the low setting where
    it draws a patch itself.
  - _The per-view buffers_ are `TerrainResources`' (`viewBuffers(view)`, `releaseView`,
    `writeFrame` and `setLighting` taking the view): the default view's made with the rest under
    R05's names, every other's at its first frame named `terrain instances (<view>)` and the
    rest; each has its own lights, and the phase table is shared. `TerrainPhaseRows.setElsewhere`
    compares the law by value (the L(α) profile by identity), so that two views' law objects
    upload the table once. A view's buffers are made in `drawFor`, which draws nothing while the
    device is lost (`EngineUnavailable`) rather than throw.
  - _The rebake rule._ The pass keeps each resident patch's `RebakeLayers` (`complete`,
    `unsurveyedCells`, `horizonRefusedCells`; `needsRebake` takes that `Pick` now) and the request
    it was last asked with (the last demand's, its rebake's, or the one held before, for a bake
    that lands outside any demand). `fieldChanged(change, settled)` asks again for every resident
    patch the rule names, drawn or not as the text says, appending them to the selection's demand
    at their last priority; the block's gate settles once each has landed in its own slot, been
    evicted, been refused by its slot or been given up (the lane's `onFailed`), and every gate
    settles at a rebuild, at the fault and at disposal.
  - _The mask's gate_ (decision D7 and §2's invariant). In `#blockTaken` the body's survey takes the
    block at once, and the GPU mask takes it at once where no pass draws the body, else in the
    gate's `settled`, which checks the body is still held at the same field epoch. The store's
    coverage (`onRevision`) is held back while a pass draws the body until the pass is settled
    **and** the workers have reported every block posted before the coverage came: the store
    answers once a payload's blocks are posted, before the workers take the last of them, so
    holding it for open rebakes alone would let it run ahead of the bakes. Mechanism: the session's
    choice (§2).
  - _The survey lookup_ (§3) is `SurveyedCells` in a module of its own, fed by every block's
    `newlySurveyed` and every store coverage at once, cleared when the workers drop the field: the
    field-level cells, and a pyramid of every coarser level holding the cells dilated by one across
    face edges and cube corners (`stepCellInto`), so that a patch no finer than the field asks one
    entry, and a finer one its cell and the neighbours across the edges and corners it touches;
    about 0.9 MB a body at level 8. `select.ts` gains `SurveyLookup`, `SelectionInput.survey`,
    `SelectedPatch.views` and `Selection.nearestSurveyM` (the least over the views of the box
    distance to the nearest patch of `NEAREST_SURVEY_LEVEL` = 8, or the finest, with surveyed
    ground under it, found best first, at least one finest patch, `+∞` with no lookup or survey).
    A bare node keeps its `seenBy`, so the 2:1 balance is unchanged, but wants nothing, is never
    forced, counts against no budget and is left out of `patches` and `demand`. `SelectedPatch`'s
    `views` and `Selection`'s `nearestSurveyM` are required (derived outputs); the two test
    fixtures that build them by hand give view 0 and `+∞`. `DrawSet` gains `views` (per drawn
    patch, the union of the views of the selected patches it draws or stands in for: a chosen patch
    drawn by its coarsest chosen ancestor gives that ancestor its views), `standingInViews` and
    `missingViews`.
  - _The contacts_ (§2). `grounded.ts` gains `GroundUnder`, `GroundUnderFunction`,
    `datumGroundUnder(figure)` (the datum's ground under a point: the parametric direction's
    spheroid point and its normal; the one function T14.c replaces) and `craftContact` (grounded
    within its held radius, as the spike's `craftContacts` rules it, or `isDescending` of its height
    and its speed along the normal; passed at the ground point at its radius). The session's
    `sceneContacts(scene, body, ground, patchM)` takes every craft of the scene: its velocity
    against the body is its own in the body's frame, less the body's retarded velocity in the
    system frame, and unknown otherwise (then it counts only while grounded); its radius its hull's
    farthest vertex (`hullBoundingRadiusM`: `TEST HULL`'s 11.06 m); at most `MAX_CONTACTS`.
  - _The session's passes._ `#stepPasses` (in `step()`, which still takes no time: each view's
    debounce takes its own draw's `nowMs`) finds the views that hand each wanted body over (T10.e's
    `terrain` regime in a photorealistic report; a wireframe view's hand-over is T11's), makes a
    body's pass at its first hand-over once its header (the pass's figure is the field header's a
    and c) and detail seed are held and its rotation known, on the first handing view's setting,
    through `this.#pool.lane(bake)` and the body's survey, and steps every pass over its handing
    views (`terrainPassViewOf`) with its contacts. A pass made while the device is lost is tried
    again at the next step. The passes are on the session's engine, not its texture wrapper, so the
    memory report's `gpuBytes` stays the masks' and maps' (asked below). Added: `passBodies`,
    `pass(body)`, `drawTerrain(view, body, input)` (T16.c's entry point), `terrainFaults` and
    `subscribeFaults`, and the pure `terrainPassViewOf`, `sceneContacts` and
    `hullBoundingRadiusM`. `#fieldReleased` disposes of the body's pass first (D4), and `dispose()`
    disposes of every pass before the rest.
  - _The fault_ (§7). `TERRAIN_NOT_AVAILABLE` is ruled's string in `annunciation.ts`. The session's
    `terrainFaults` holds every view that hands a body over while `lostWorkers === workerCount`,
    a new set only when it changes, which `useTerrainFaults(session)` follows with
    `useSyncExternalStore`; `faultsFor` puts it after `faultFor`'s graphics fault; `ViewLabelBlock`
    and `InstrumentView` take `faults`, each its own `StatusLine` fault line. A faulted pass asks
    for nothing (`reprioritise([])` once), draws an empty draw set, and gives every view's frame the
    fault with a `null` annunciation and `maskReady` false.
  - _`RebakeLayers` leaves out `horizonComplete`_ (the batch review's S23): `needsRebake` does not
    read it, which is `staleInFlight`'s, so the pass keeps `complete`, `unsurveyedCells` and
    `horizonRefusedCells` alone.
  - _The pass reads no `waitingCount`_ (S23): a patch waiting for a block of its surveyed region has
    no resident bake, so its view's draw set counts it missing or standing in, which raises
    `TERRAIN: STREAMING` as the text's "(the lane's `waitingCount`) do count" asks; the test holds a
    patch not yet baked.
  - _The mask at cell code 0_ (decision-r10-t16-review §2; built in the batch review's fixes, F1).
    `maskReadyFor(id)` and `drawFor(id, …).maskReady` are false while the view sees a drawn patch,
    selected or standing in, of cell code 0 (`surveyCellCode(level, fieldLevel) === 0`, six or more
    levels coarser than the field) whose last bake's `unsurveyedCells` is not empty; nothing else
    changes (`missingViews`, `standingInViews`, the annunciation, its debounce, the demand and the
    budget). The invariant, restated: wherever the mask is given, each cell the GPU mask holds
    surveyed lies under a drawn patch whose bake draws it, at code 1 or more by the cell's centre
    vertex, at code 0 by every vertex surveyed. Its cost: on the fixture (field level 6, the roots
    alone of code 0) the mask is withheld for the one bake round after each start from an empty
    cache in which a root stands in (the first hand-over, a restore, `VIEW` shown again), the
    reference surface whole beneath it. The error it removes: a strip up to a root quad wide (a
    level-6 cell, about 39 km) where neither surface drew and the sky showed through, about 3 px at
    τ 1 and 6 px at τ 2 at the hand-over range and wider than the view at 4 km. Tested by the
    ruling's four in `terrainPassShared.test.ts` (F1's record).
  - _`Selection`'s shape since F1_ (decision-r10-t16-review §3; the batch review's S9): each view's
    own `nearestSurveyByViewM`, `nearestSurveyM` their least as before, under §3's conditions for

- **Questions for "main" (R10.T16.b)** (none touches a contract of the server's; each built to its
  lean). _Main's ruling: the cell-code-0 question ruled (decision-r10-t16-review §2, below); the
  others none relayed to the lane by F2 (2026-10-20); the lane lead marks each here as main rules
  it._
  - _The mask's coverage gate goes beyond the ruling's words._ The store's coverage waits for the
    workers' report of the blocks posted before it as well as for the rebakes (above). Lean: as
    built; without it the mask runs ahead of the bakes for a frame or more at every payload. _Ruled
    (decision-r10-t16-leans §13): accepted._
  - _Every resident patch the rule names is baked again, drawn or not, and the gate waits for all_
    (the text's "for each resident patch"). Lean: as built; T14 may evict an undrawn one instead
    (deferred below). _Ruled (decision-r10-t16-leans §13): accepted; T14 weighs eviction instead._
  - _A craft's velocity in another body's frame is not judged_ (a craft descending to a moon while
    held in its planet's frame): it is a contact only once grounded. Lean: as built until the
    flight model gives craft velocities against any body; T14.c with the workers' ground. _Ruled
    (decision-r10-t16-leans §13): accepted until T14.c, which chains the frames._
  - _The session's memory report leaves out the passes' GPU bytes_ (64–400 MB each). Lean: R12 reads
    the engine's tally by category (`height-cache` is the passes' alone in `VIEW`) beside the report;

    (decision-r10-t16-leans §13): accepted, recorded in R12's Consumes._
  - _The mask at cell code 0_ (the batch review's S21, moved here from the deferred findings): the
    invariant held at code 0 by T10.c's interpolated half alone. Lean: such patches are drawn where
    a cell is about a pixel. _Ruled (decision-r10-t16-review §2): not as drawn; the lean's bound
    does not hold (R05's streaming gate draws the roots first at every start from an empty cache,
    at whatever range the camera holds), so the view's mask is withheld while it sees a drawn
    code-0 patch with a vertex outside the survey (above, built by F1)._
- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule) (R10.T16.b)** (recorded, not ruled; each leaves the
  algorithm and the contracts as built).
  - _The mask withheld at cell code 0_ (decision-r10-t16-review §2). On a field of level 7 or 8,
    levels 0–2 withhold the mask for as many bake rounds; where such a level is a steady leaf inside
    the hand-over range, it withholds it over a range of distances, the reference surface standing
    over surveyed valleys there. Within a whole code-0 patch on such a field, an unsurveyed cell
    lying between surveyed vertices is drawn by both surfaces, under a quad wide. The lever is
    T10.e's: the terrain's discard reads the GPU coverage mask where its code is 0, so that the mask
    can be given there. The trigger: T15's descent on a served world of field level 7 or 8, or
    T4.b's statistical bound making a code-0 level a steady leaf inside the hand-over range.
  - _Undrawn rebakes cost worker time_, and delay the mask until they land, at every block that
    names cached patches no view draws. T14 measures it beside "The live path's costs".
  - ~~_The default view's buffers in every pass._~~ Retired by the batch review's C4 (F1): every
    view's buffers, the default's (now `""`) included, are made at its first frame.
  - _`nearestSurveyM` runs at every selection with a survey_ (a best-first descent of a few tens of
    patches a view): unmeasured, small beside a selection.
  - _A wireframe view hands nothing over until T11_, so it shows no terrain fault line either.

    record's lights', occluders' and planetshine sources' directions and centres taken by Rᵀ
    (`rotateToBodyFixed`), every distance, radius, illuminance and annulus as it stands,
    `elsewhere` the record's surface's first law (`discSurfaceLaws`: the uniform law or the class
    map's unsurveyed ground's, unscaled, as `packTerrainLighting` scales it), and the frame's
    pre-exposure; the sun the record's first light (`lightsAt` puts the brightest first), `+z` and
    zero illuminance with none (R05's spike shading alone reads them).
  - _`FrameTerrain.draws(plan, bodies)`_ (beyond the text's `draws(plan)`). A `BodyFramePlan`
    carries no body's centre or rotation (a `DiscRecord` holds a unit direction and a ÷ D, not the
    `f64` centre), so the renderer passes the frame's `LitBodyInput`s, the inputs the plan was made

    `cameraM` `scale(centreM, −1)`, tested bit for bit with `Object.is`; the camera's orientation
    and field of view; the presented size). `FrameTerrain` also gains `symbologyDepth()` (below).
  - _The mask before the plan._ `litBodiesOf` asks `surveyCoverage(body)` before the frame's plan,
    which takes the mask, exists; the session's step precedes every view's draw, so the draw set
    is fixed then. `TerrainPass.maskReadyFor(id)` gives `drawFor`'s `maskReady` from the last
    step alone: the view taken, nothing it sees missing, and wherever it sees a patch the material

    needs the draw made, so the two differ only for a draw refused at its making (a device lost
    within the frame). `LiveFrameTerrain.surveyCoverage` gives `coverageMask(body)` only then.
  - _Per view, per frame._ `ViewFrameInputs.terrain` is a `ViewTerrainInput`
