- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule) (R10.T16.c)** (recorded, not ruled; each leaves the
  algorithm and the contracts as built).
  - _The edge's cost a frame._ Every view's draw list marks every wanted body's edge in view every
    frame, each point now with a rim lookup (a level walk of at most some twenty map reads) and the
    note's march (32 lookups a candidate, nearest first): unmeasured; a survey of thousands of
    cells seen from low over it could cost milliseconds. T14 measures it beside "The live path's
    costs"; the levers are a mark kept while the camera and the bakes stand still, and fewer
    pieces off the view.
  - _The depth raster's cost._ Each handed-over body's drawn patches are rastered twice in each
    photorealistic view, the second time at the canvas's resolution, depth alone (its fragments
    the discard and a depth write). T14.
  - _The ground's coarse copy_ misses ridges narrower than four quads of a wholly surveyed patch,
    a few pixels where it is drawn, and the bilinear heights are not the drawn triangles (1 m of
    tolerance): a point hidden or shown by a few pixels may count either way.
  - _The edge marks the store's coverage_, which may trail the blocks the workers took by the
    store's answer: for that while the terrain draws newly surveyed cells whose edge still stands at
    the old survey's line. _(F2, the batch review's C8:)_ it can also run ahead of the GPU mask's
    cells while a pass holds the store's coverage back from the mask (T16.b's gate, D7): for that
    while the edge stands at the new survey's line over ground the reference surface still draws.
  - _The depth push over grazing ground_ (the batch review's C6, for T11 and T12, where the edge is
    read low over the survey): about 1.8 × 10⁻³ × cot(grazing angle) of the range at 1080p across
    60°, so 492 m at 100 m up 5 km out and 15.6 km at 10 km up grazing 2° at 287 km; a mark that
    far behind the ground shows through it. The rule is every occluder's (R07.T16.d); the lever, a
    push bounded in metres or by the slope's own depth range, is T11's and T12's to weigh.
  - _The annunciation reaches the label block at the readout rate_, up to 250 ms after the
    debounce's 250 ms onset, as every reading does.
  - _At a hand-over's first or last frame_ the note's ground follows the pass's last step, which
    may differ from the frame's plan by one frame.
  - _A handed-over body's footprint_ in the promotion is its equatorial sphere's; its terrain may
    stand past it by its relief over its radius (5 × 10⁻⁴ of the disc on the Moon-like world),
    where a disc behind is not promoted.
  - _The surveyed body's occluder at its polar radius_ (T10.c's deferred): over the image the band
    between it and the equatorial limb is now covered where the terrain is drawn, and still open
    over the reference surface.

      `SURVEY COVERAGE REJECTED: <the server's reason>, reopen VIEW to retry` in its place until
      the field is asked for afresh, and the view states no contours or terrain readout over it",
      and its row: `SURVEY COVERAGE REJECTED` | Status | A view's survey line while the server
      refuses the body's field, with the server's reason and the retry, steady and in `--text`:
      `SURVEY COVERAGE REJECTED: <reason>, reopen VIEW to retry`.
    - _Data the client cannot read_, a fault, as `BODY DATA INVALID` is: "Where the body's field
      fails the client's checks, the line reads
      `SURVEY DATA INVALID: <the check that failed>, reopen VIEW to retry` in its place, a fault in
      `--status-caution`, until the field is asked for afresh", and the row's family gaining it: `SYSTEM DATA INVALID`, `BODY DATA INVALID` |
      Fault | …, also `SURVEY DATA INVALID` for a view's survey line.
    - The forms, chosen deliberately: the label block's colon form, `STATE: sentence`, as
      `TERRAIN: STREAMING` and `TERRAIN NOT AVAILABLE: …` are set (Typography: the state tracked,
      the sentence after the colon not); `REJECTED` and `DATA INVALID` over `NOT AVAILABLE`, since
      each names its cause where `NOT AVAILABLE` names none, and joins its family's rows. The
      retry is reopening `VIEW`, since the session asks every field afresh when it is made again
      (decision D8). Both steady: neither is an alert (the guide's Alerts: a console's own report
      is never one). ASCII alone, so the glyph check has nothing to flag.

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule) (R10.T16.d, part 1)** (recorded, not ruled; each leaves the
  algorithm and the contracts as built).
  - _`TEST MOON`'s photometry against its field's._ Its uniform law is its primary crust's
    (feldspathic, A_N 0.20 under the Regolith row), where its field's maria (`basalt_fe`, 0.10)
    cover some 4 to 5 per cent of it by their closed forms and its consolidated forms take
    Lambert's law, and its cold traps' H2O ice (A_N 0.965) a small area; and the field's header
    carries no albedo scale (`albedo_scale: null`), so the
    surveyed ground draws the palette's albedos as resolved (c = 1). Off the survey its disc and
    figure are then a few per cent brighter than an area-weighted mix of its materials; the survey
    itself is highland, so no step shows at its edge from the crust alone. The lever: the header's
    p from R10.T10.a's solve over the field's class fractions (`class_fractions`), pinned in the
    golden. _Ruled (decision-r10-t16d-part1, finding (a)): deferred; the maria alone make the disc
    about 2.5% bright (p ≈ 0.195 against 0.20), under Design note 5's 5% tolerance; the lever goes to
    whoever next re-blesses `terrain_test.golden`, or to T15._
  - _The interim stars asked again._ `TERRAIN TEST`'s system is not `KEPT_SYSTEM`, so a switch
    between it and another kept scene asks the four `systems_in_range` again (`useInterimStars`
    keys its arrival by system), though the queries are the same. _Ruled (finding (b)): deferred,
    for R02 (`useInterimStars`)._
  - _The ship's speed high up_, about 32 km/s of scene time at the descent's fastest (31.5 km/s
    radial at about 23 s of the script, some 51,000 km up, plus about 3.4 km/s of co-rotation;
    decision-r10-t16d-part1, finding (c), correcting 24 km/s), at the script's 60 s/s: a scripted
    path, not a flight; no readout shows it (the mark list's closure is craft to craft); the
    descent from 80,000 km would take about a day at a lunar transfer's speeds. _Ruled: accepted;
    for T12, a readout of the own ship's speed or vertical rate would show this figure truthfully
    on `TERRAIN TEST`._

    `createMaterial` material whose pipeline is made synchronously on the GPU process's main thread
    at its first draw, the body's first frame in T10.e's `terrain` regime
    (`DeviceBase::APICreateRenderPipeline`, 1,547 ms); high's 1.45 s is the same switch, not
    traced. VIEW's opening stalls the same way for `bodies:disc` (1,128 ms) and `bodies:discLimb`
    (1,093 ms). The levers are T14.d's, as amended._

    is split for every view that sees it: a primary settled 2,000 km over a pole announces
    `TERRAIN: STREAMING` for a bake round when an instrument joins over the equator, the faces'
    roots it sees by their boxes split for the instrument. As designed (decision-r10-t16-contracts
    §3); for T14, beside "The live path's costs" (the lever, a split taken only for the views that
    want it, where the 2:1 balance allows).

    variant without a ship, reaches the stage's bottom edge, its plate's last padding cut, every

- **Deviations in T16.e, as built** (2026-10-20; lane r10-readouts, on `rendering-and-planets` at
  `1870973b`; decision-r10-t16-leans §8 and §11).
  - _The fault._ `annunciation.ts` gains `TERRAIN_COMPUTATION_FAILED` beside
    `TERRAIN_NOT_AVAILABLE`, the type `TerrainFault` of the two and `isTerrainFault`. A new
    `view/terrain/failureGuard.ts`, `TerrainFailureGuard.run` (the call, its fallback, the frame's
    time and the report's `describe` and `onFault`), guards each call: a success clears it; a loss
    (`EngineUnavailable`) passes in silence, neither starting nor clearing a run of failures; any
    other throw is reported by `console.error` once a run, and `onFault` is called once the run has
    lasted `ANNUNCIATION_ONSET_MS`, so one failed frame raises nothing. `stepTerrainSession` (the
    session, its guard and the frame's time) guards the session's step in `VIEW`'s loop, and the
    drawer's `#surveyEdges` its own guard with `ViewTerrainInput.nowMs`; each takes a new guard
    when the session changes, so that one session's run of failures never counts against the next.
  - _The session._ `TerrainSession.failComputation()`, sticky: every pass halted
    (`TerrainPass.halt(cause)`, the private fault R10.T16.b built, now with its cause, which
    `drawFor` reports) and none made again; the faults raised at once, not at the next step, which
    may be what throws (where the views that hand a body over cannot be told either, every view that
    has reported is faulted). `terrainFaults` is a `ReadonlyMap<ViewId, TerrainFault>`, the text the
    session's first cause raised, which stands for the session: lost workers'
    `TERRAIN_NOT_AVAILABLE`, or the computation's. After the fault each step follows the fields and
    the fault and steps no pass. Lost workers alone behave as built. The masks are withheld for a
    halted pass and for a body never given one, and the annunciations are `null`, as with lost
    workers. `viewFaults.ts`' `faultsFor` appends the view's text; `terrainStatementOf` and the
    primary's statement drop the terrain annunciation under either text (`isTerrainFault`; inline in
    `ViewDisplay`, where a call to `terrainStatementOf` drew oxlint's React-compiler errors).
  - _The survey edge on a faulted pass (found in the build, fixed here)._ `surveyEdgeViewsOf` stood
    the rim on a faulted pass's resident heights while the view drew the body's figure, since the
    pass keeps its last step's views: true of lost workers since T16.b. `FrameTerrainPass` gains
    `faulted`, and a faulted pass draws no ground, so the rim stands on the datum, as for a view
    that hands the body to no pass.
  - _The run._ The probe follows the session's `subscribeFaults` in `watchTerrain` and records each
    change to a held fault (`TerrainCheckSessionFault`: its time, text and views) in the record's
    `terrainFaults`. Main's results gain the finding "No terrain fault (the session's terrainFaults
    never held a view)", a failure for each record, in the overall verdict, its table row and its
    JSON member; `TERRAIN_CHECK_VERSION` 2, as its own comment asks for any change of shape.
  - _The banner._ `App.tsx`'s `modeBanner` is `MEASUREMENT` whenever `window.hyperion.viewsCheck`
    is present, on every display, for the whole launch; `TRAINING` otherwise as built.
  - _The guide._ The `TERRAIN NOT AVAILABLE` row's second cause (§8), and the `TRAINING` and
    `MEASUREMENT` rows (§11), as the ruling gives them; nothing else. The `SCENE` row's "under the
    training banner" stands, which the `TRAINING` row's exception now covers (§15 C).
  - _Tests._ The guard (a single throw, a run under and over 250 ms, a loss, the report once); the
    session (a step throwing for 250 ms faults each handing view and stops the terrain, no demand,
    no draw, the mask withheld, no annunciation; a single throw does not; the first cause stands);
    the label block's fault line through `VIEW`; the survey edges' guard in the drawer; the rim on a
    faulted pass; `MEASUREMENT` on F1 to F4 on a views-check launch, T20's and the terrain run's;
    a terrain fault fails main's verdict and the launch exits 1. The console-ux checks: `ux_lint.py`
    on the changed renderer files, 0 errors; `glyphs.py` on the new string, all ASCII;
    `contrast.py status-caution surface-0` 12.01:1.

    `page.ts`, `terrain.ts`, `litTerrain.ts` and `surveyEdge.ts` (`normalsAtlasOf`); and tests
    beside each. No wire format, payload, Rust code, guide text or golden changes.
  - _The shading_ (D10's "a pass of its own shading"). `TerrainShading` gains `wire`, a body's
    bakes with `weights: "skipped"` (`terrainShadingOf`; T6.b's and T8.b's skipped layers), and
    each place the shadings differ reads `TERRAIN_SHADING_TRAITS` (normals, the lit fields, the
    survey mask, the lit mesh, the phases, the low setting's coarser detail), so that a fourth
    shading is a compile error until its traits are given. Its slot holds the heights, the offsets
    on their path and the `survey-mask` field T10.c's lit slot holds, nothing else: 38,028 B on
    `face-differences`, 139,428 B on `baked-offsets` (the task's "heights and mask only", the
    vertex path's offsets beside them). So it has no normals atlas (`WireTerrainLayout`, whose
    `atlas` is `null`; `normalsAtlasOf` the lit and spike layouts' reader), and the bake's normals,
    which the worker still makes, are not kept (deferred below). It draws the lit material's mesh
    (`litPatchMeshData`, 190,644 B under `other` a pass, where decision-r10-t16-contracts §1
    foresaw R05's spike mesh, 158,268 B), whose skirts and fins close the terrain's depth to the
    occluder sphere at the survey's edge, and each view has a phases buffer beside its instances
    (`WirePhaseRecords`, 48 B a drawn patch).
  - _The cache, sized by its slots_ (beyond the text, which names no budget; T14 decides; _Ruled
    (decision-r10-view-block-room §8): kept at 520, provisional_). `WIREFRAME_TERRAIN_SLOTS` = 520
    on both settings (`wireframeTerrainSettings`), 19.8 MB on the low setting and 72.5 MB on the
    high, its selection budget half of it, 260 patches (decision-r05-patch-demand.md, 4b). The
    figure is Design note 15's sizing rule over its wireframe column, max(1.3 × 284, 3 × 76) ≈ 370
    at 100 m, with the 40% the count model leaves out for relief, the 2:1 rule and the forced
    region; it was read without the budget's halving. The setting's own bytes would have given
    2,868 slots on the high setting's `baked-offsets`, whose offsets pass a default 128 MiB storage
    binding, and 10,518 on its fallback, whose heights do too. Measured in `TERRAIN TEST`'s descent
    (the hidden look's selection every 10 s of the script, the primary alone): the 260 bind from
    80–90 s to the script's end on both settings, the refused split's weighted excess rising to 28
    on low and 33 on high, the stand-ins settled within a bake round (48 at most). With a scratch
    build of 3,000 slots (1,500 patches; about 114 MB on low and 418 MB on high) they still bind,
    from 100 s to 220 s on low with the excess to 7.1 and from 140 s to 210 s on high with it to
    9.9, and the bakes stand in for most of the descent (on low 1,395 at 90 s, settled at 160 s,
    about 21 bakes a second; on high 1,477 at 130 s and 743 still at 180 s, about 11 a second on
    `baked-offsets`). So no cache of a few hundred
    megabytes leaves the descent unlimited at 4 px, and a larger one trades `DETAIL LIMITED` for
    `STREAMING` at the pool's rate, on high a `STREAMING` that never clears; at 520 `STREAMING`
    clears within a round and `DETAIL LIMITED` is true. The 520 stand, provisional, for T14
    (deferred below: the selection's demand on R09's moon).
  - _The pass_ (`terrainPass.ts`). A wireframe pass compiles `terrainWireMaterialSpec(path)` for
    the canvas, which the wireframe's frame draws into; `TerrainFrameInput.wire`
    (`TerrainWireFrameInput`: the interval, the sea level or `null`, the stroke scale, the
    graticule's step and widths or `null`, the colours and the slope term) is what each view's draw
    takes, and with none a wireframe pass draws nothing. Each drawn patch's phase record, in the
    instances' order: φ = h₀ mod 5 CI (`contourPhase`) from the bake's origin height as its slot
    record narrows it, h₀ less the sea level, and its place for the graticule
    (`graticulePatch(originM, step)`, kept for the resident patch until the step changes). Its
    `TERRAIN: DETAIL LIMITED` is the selection's budget alone: the low setting's clause
    (`setting === "low" && count > 0`, Design note 26) is not taken (the shading's
    `coarserOnLow`), since R05's note has the low setting say it "whenever terrain is in view" for
    the photorealistic style's coarser τ and resolution, and the brainstorm's rule, "whenever the
    setting draws the surface below the detail the camera's position warrants" (Two styles of one
    renderer), is never met by the wireframe, whose τ and presented size are the same on both
    settings. The mask rule (`maskReadyFor`, `drawFor`'s `maskReady`) is the lit pass's, the code-0
    rule included (decision-r10-t16-review §2, the task's pointer), with no phase table to wait
    for. The craft's contacts are written for its draw as for the lit one's, so that the ground
    under a grounded craft holds its morph at zero (`terrainPassWire.test.ts`).
  - _The hand-over in the wireframe_ (the lane lead's decision; the text's "selected at 4 px over
    the wireframe views that hand the body over"). A wireframe frame plans no regimes, so the
    session judges it at each step from the view's report (`wireframeHandovers`, pure): each lit
    body of its scene with a rotation whose relief (`HandoverReliefSource.reliefM`) subtends
    `handoverTauPx("wireframe")`, 4 px, at its limb from the camera at the presented size's centre
    pixel, with R07's hysteresis (`handsOver`, from the bodies the view handed over at its last
    step), for a view whose budget's style and last frame are both the wireframe's: a
    photorealistic view standing in with the wireframe hands nothing over, as T16's S8 has it. The
    first such hand-over makes the body's wireframe pass, through a lane of the session's one pool
    (`HeightWorkerPool.lane`) with its `frustumMargin` of `motion`, stepped over the wireframe
    views that hand the body over with the scene's contacts, and disposed with the lit pass where
    the workers drop the field (D4). A body may have both passes, on one pool, and then holds both
    caches, the lit setting's budget and the wireframe's (Risks, "The live terrain path's costs"):
    the GPU mask takes a block's cells once every pass that draws the body has its rebakes
    (`#blockTaken`), and the store's coverage once every pass is settled (`#flushCoverage`). Every
    wireframe view that hands a body over takes `TERRAIN_NOT_AVAILABLE` with every worker lost, as
    T16.b's fault has it. Added: `wirePass(body)`, `drawWireTerrain(view, body, input)`,
    `wirePassBodies`.
  - _The frame_ (`frameTerrain.ts`' `wireframeTerrainOf`; the text's "its draw joins each wireframe
    view's `WireframeRenderer.render` through the session"). For each body whose wireframe pass
    took the view in its last step: its `TerrainView` from the scene's body (its rotation, its
    centre from the camera negated), its draw with the frame's `wire`, its annunciation (the more
    pressing), and, where the draw may take the mask (`maskReady`), the body's coverage mask. One
    interval for the view (the label block states one): `contourInterval` of the camera's height
    above the ground at its nadir (`heightAboveGroundM`: along the spheroid's normal, less the
    wireframe pass's `ResidentHeights.groundHeightAtM` at the nadir's parametric direction, the
    datum where none is drawn) over the body it stands lowest over, from the view's last
    (`ViewFrameDrawer`'s held interval, each view's hysteresis its own until R10.T12.b, below). The
    graticule's step
    and widths are R02's for the body's apparent size (`graticuleStepDeg`, `bodyRegime`: none in
    the limb regime), so that the terrain's graticule continues the datum's. The sea level is the
    header's `sea_level_m` where the header names a main liquid (`main_liquid`), and no coastline
    otherwise (the header's sea level on a world with no sea is its lowest cell's).
    `WireframeRenderer.frame` takes it (`WireframeTerrain`): the terrain's draws after every
    occluder, so that a nearer body or hull hides its contours, and before the background and the
    lines, which its depth hides.
  - _The datum gives way to the terrain_ (beyond the text; Design note 12's "so no terrain is
    claimed there and no reference surface shows through a surveyed valley", carried into the
    wireframe). In the wireframe the reference surface is the body's occluder sphere and its own
    lines, its limb and graticule on the datum. Where a view's draw of the body takes its mask,
    both are discarded over every cell the GPU mask holds surveyed (`occluderSphereSurveyed`,
    `DATUM OCCLUDER`; `linesSurveyed`, `DATUM LINES`, for the batches that carry `LineBatch.body`;
    both read the mask through `wireCoverage.wgsl`, the hit's or the stroke's point stretched along
    the pole as R07's figure reads it), so that no datum line floats over a surveyed valley and the
    sphere hides none of it. While the mask is withheld (anything missing, or a code-0 patch drawn)
    both stand whole, as the reference surface does in the photorealistic style.
  - _The contours_ (Design note 14 as signed off, signoff-9). Depth with colour only on its lines:
    minor 1 px and index 1.5 px in `--text-muted`, the coastline 2 px in `--text`, each in CSS px
    times the view's stroke scale, uncased; antialiased from the screen gradient's length; a
    family drawn in full from 6 px of spacing and gone at 3 px, the minor first; no line on the
    skirts or fins, which are the ground's depth alone. The height varies patch-local, h − h₀ for
    the slot record's own h₀, both `f32`. Two departures from the note's arithmetic: φ is
    h₀ mod 5 CI, the index's period, rather than mod CI, so that the index contour is told from the
    minor ones; and the coordinate is (h − h₀ + φ) × (1 ÷ CI), 1 ÷ CI formed in `f64`, since WGSL
    rounds a product correctly where it allows a quotient 2.5 ULP. The tests hold the coordinate to
    the `f64` levels within 1 mm at ±20 km (`terrainWire.test.ts`, the phase's two tests, at WGSL's
    bounds); the lane's emulation over the same points measured 0.24 mm with the product against
    1.19 mm with the quotient at a 1 km interval. The depth is pushed away by the occluders' rule
    (R07.T16.d: `occluderSlopePx` pixels of its slope and 2⁻¹⁶ of the depth), so that the survey
    edge on its rim stands in front of the ground it lies on.
  - _The graticule on the terrain_ (Design note 14's "R02's graticule is drawn over the terrain's
    height where terrain is surveyed"). The terrain's fragment draws it: its parallels (not the
    poles) and meridians at R02's step, the equator and the prime meridian at the heavy width, by
    the terrain point's geocentric latitude and longitude, as R02's sphere graticule takes them
    (`bodies.ts`' `unitAt`), cased in `--surface-0` as R02's lines are (the lane lead's choice; its
    casing cuts the contours where it crosses them). Each vertex's latitude and longitude less its
    patch origin's are formed from its offset in a form that takes no difference of nearly equal
    numbers (`graticuleOffsetsRad`, `wire_graticule_offsets`), through `preciseTrig.wgsl`'s
    `preciseAtan2` rather than WGSL's `atan2`, bounded only to 4,096 ULP, and the origin's own
    less its nearest lines' in `f64` on the CPU. The tests hold a fine patch's lines in `f32`, at
    every corner of WGSL's bounds, within 2 × 10⁻⁹ rad of arc of the truth for offsets up to 2 km,
    and show the absolute position's `f32` latitude erring past 2 × 10⁻⁸ rad over the same points;
    the emulation measured 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ rad correctly rounded and 3.7 × 10⁻¹⁰ at WGSL's bounds,
    against 9.8 × 10⁻⁸ rad for the absolute position, some 0.6 m on an Earth.
  - _The survey edge in the wireframe_ (T16.c's S1 interim ended). `surveyEdgeViewsOf` takes the
    rim and the note's ground from the wireframe pass's resident heights where it took the view,
    as from the lit pass's in the photorealistic style; the edge is drawn over the terrain's own
    depth, which hides it behind nearer ground.

    `labelLines(run, exposure, stale, contourIntervalM)` states
    `CONTOUR INTERVAL 200 m · INDEX 1 km` directly after `FOV`, the picture's other scale, while
    the view draws contours
    (`ViewFrameDrawn.contourIntervalM`), not stale, being the picture's statement of scale. The
    plan names `labelStatements`; the interval is a label and its value (the guide's
    `CONTOUR INTERVAL` row, kind `Label`), so it is a `labelLines` line (`contourIntervalLine`),
    drawn by the same `ViewLabelBlock.tsx`. The interval stands in a field of 8 ch
    (`CONTOUR_FIELD_CH`, its longest reading `10000 km`: 40 km of relief handed over through a 10°
    field on a 3,840 px canvas, some 220,000 km out), so that `· INDEX` never moves as the
    interval steps (the guide's "Numbers"); the index ends the line with no field, since nothing
    follows it to move (where the line is its plate's widest, the plate is a character narrower or
    wider as the index changes unit); and the line's middle dot leads the index's part
    (`dotsLead`, as the sky's `STARS` line has it). One departure from the ruling's "the
    `INDEX 2.5 km` run stays unbroken": the index's part may break before its value, as it does
    beside an open slot at 1280 × 720, where the block sets the line on three rows, `500 m`,
    `· INDEX` and `2.5 km` (`500 m ·`, `INDEX` and `2.5 km` with the dot between the parts), since
    its column there, about 114 px, is narrower than the part's 128 px, which would otherwise run
    past the plate's edge; there the leading dot keeps `INTERVAL` and `INDEX`, side by side on the
    second row, from reading as one label. Two deviations until R10.T12.b, which builds both with
    its held slot: a wireframe instrument draws its contours without stating its interval (the
    `PRIMARY` view's block alone states one; on today's slot rule the line would carry slot 2 about
    56 px past the stage at the floor), and each view holds its own interval for Design note 14's
    ±20% hysteresis, so two views at one pose that reached it from different heights could state
    intervals a step apart, where the guide has "every view in one pose states the same one" (no
    instrument states one yet, so none is seen to differ). A wireframe instrument states its own
    terrain annunciation and fault.
  - _The views check_ (T16.d's hidden run). The probe counts a frame as drawing the terrain by

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule) (R10.T11)** (recorded, not ruled; each leaves the algorithm
  and the contracts as built).
  - _The selection's demand on R09's moon_ (decision-r10-view-block-room §8). At 4 px the
    wireframe's selection over `TERRAIN TEST` binds a budget of 1,500 patches with a weighted excess
    of 7 to 10 (the cache, above), more than twenty times Design note 15's 76 in the frustum at
    100 m on an Earth; the lit style's, at 1 or 2 px and its own budget, binds harder. The scene's
    clock runs at 60 s/s, and the frustum margin `motion` sets from the camera's motion a frame
    widens the selection with it. For T14: the count model's motion margin at a scene clock above
    1 s/s; a measurement at 1 s/s, the game's own rate; the wireframe's budget sized from that,
    with these figures and the 520's derivation (the cache, above); and the selection's error
    bounds on R09's relief against the model's premise.
  - _The wireframe's share on R05's golden level table_ (decision-r10-view-block-room §9). Design
    note 15's wireframe column assumes r ≈ 0.26 at k = 5 edges, while the golden table's k ≈ 15
    gives 0.070 to 0.115 at 1, 10 and 100 km; beside the absolute count above, twenty times the
    frustum figure, the note's wireframe sizing is off both ways. T14.a's `patchCountModel` and
    T14.b measure it, and the brainstorm's "about a fifth" waits on them.
  - _Two caches on one pool, and one view's slots._ A body handed over in both styles holds the
    lit setting's cache and the wireframe's at once (19.8–72.5 MB more), and the 520 slots are one
    view's, where Design note 15 sums over the views that stream (two wireframe instruments at one
    position share its all-round term). For T14.b.
  - _Normals baked for nothing._ A wireframe bake still makes its normals, and the slot drops
    them. The lever: a skipped-normals bake setting beside the weights' (T6.b's worker).
  - _Contours in pieces near the horizon._ Where a family's spacing on screen passes through the
    fade's 6 to 3 px along a line, judged pixel by pixel, and nearer ground hides it in places,
    far contours break into short pieces (high `between-wire-248s`, `between-wire-north-220s`); in
    the captures they read as fragments of the ground's lines rather than dashes, which the guide
    reserves for predictions. The lever: the fade judged from a smoother measure of the spacing
    (the patch's gradient, or the screen gradient over a coarser footprint).
  - _No small body seen._ `TERRAIN TEST`'s moon is the only surveyed scene, so the legibility
    check's "on a small body too" was not seen; for the first kept scene or served system with a
    surveyed small body (T15's verification pass).
  - _The views check's patch counts._ The probe's phase table counts the lit pass's patches alone
    (its `view:hdr` frames), so a wireframe-only run records none; for the views check's next
    revision.

    `{ heightM, fovXRad, frustumMarginRad? }` over `COUNT_MODEL_SITE` (face 0, level 19,

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule) (R10.T14.a)** (recorded, not ruled unless marked; each
  leaves the algorithm and the contracts as built).
  - _R05's box margin along the normal._ _Ruled (decision-r10-t14a, the #56 follow-up): fixed by
    R10.T14.e._ The bounds' ring-chord margin on the normal's half-extent (`packPatchBounds`) lets
    `aboveHorizon` pass coarse patches wholly below the true horizon, which selection then selects,
    demands, bakes and draws: at 100 m on the count model's premise, 654 of the high setting's
    3,014 all-round leaves, 178 of low's 581 and 125 of the wireframe's 409, the boxes' all-round
    counts 1.15–1.44 times the exact across the table. `bounds.ts` is untouched here; T14.e takes
    the chord's sagitta along the normal and re-pins what moves, this task's box-metric table and
    the replay's pinned peaks among them.
  - _The relief's tall boxes._ At ±24.5 km the frustum peak is 3.8–8.8 times the smooth sphere's,
    two thirds of the all-round count: an unbaked patch's box spans its level's whole height range,
    and a view sees boxes by their bottoms. Real bakes' ranges shrink it; T14.b measures it on a
    generated world, with the bound ratio and box heights it logs.
  - _The high setting's rule past the ceiling._ On the model's boxes even the frustum rule (2,009
    slots) passes the 1,323 a default binding holds on `baked-offsets`, so a budget set from it
    puts the high setting on `face-differences` on adapters at the defaults. For T14.b.
  - _The low cache's pins._ At 422 lit slots, half of them the budget, the descent's pins fill the
    low cache in 136 of its 723 contact frames under the levels' height ranges (the backstop's
    report). T14.b measures on real bakes.
  - _`terrainWireSelection.test.ts`' stale remark._ Its module doc says `patchCountModel` is not
    built; the file stays as it is (R4), for T14.b, which may hold its bracket to the model's
    ratios.
- **Questions for main (R10.T14.a)**
  1. _The band's horizon_ (asked on the issue, not blocking; answered). The model as ruled
     reproduces `selectPatches` (1.000–1.007), but on its boxes' horizon six of the high column's
     cells pass test 3's [0.5, 2] (×2.02–2.21). The lean, that the model reports both horizons and

     accepted, with the exact horizon made exact rather than sampled (Amendment A) and R05's margin
     fixed by R10.T14.e, not here (Amendment B)._ Both are built and recorded above.
- **Deviations in T14.e, as built** (2026-10-20; lane `lane/57-r10-t14e-box-margin`, on
  `rendering-and-planets` at `ae4bd052`; decision-r10-t14a's #56 follow-up).
  - _Files._ Changed: `view/terrain/bounds.ts` and `bounds.test.ts`; the pins in
    `view/spike/demandRecord.test.ts`, `view/terrain/select.test.ts`, `cacheBudget.test.ts` and
    `cache.test.ts`; `cacheBudget.ts`' `PatchCountModel` doc alone; and plan 05's pointer in
    R05.T7.a's record. No wire, protocol, DTO, golden, generator version or Rust change;
    `select.ts`, `cull.ts` and the rest of the brief's "don't change" list are untouched, and the
    ranges fixture is as it was. New in `bounds.ts`: `normalMarginM`, of the angle bound, a, c and
    H, `NORMAL_BEND_FACTOR` (1.155) and `ROUNDING_ALLOWANCE_EPSILONS` (64).
    `PATCH_GEOMETRY_LENGTH` grows from 408 to 411 numbers, which `select.ts` allocates by.
  - _The bound as built._ The normal's half-extent is half the samples' span along ν_c plus
    δ = (Θ² ÷ 8)(a + K H a² ÷ c²) + 64 ε (a + H), with Θ² bounded by q² ÷ (1 − q² ÷ 4) for q the
    largest chord between neighbouring ring samples' unit directions (Θ = 2 asin(q ÷ 2) and
    asin x ≤ x ÷ √(1 − x²)), K = 1.155 ≥ 2 ÷ √3, H the range's largest |h| and ε = 2⁻⁵². The
    tangents' half-extents and the sphere's radius keep the chord, unchanged to the bit, as do the
    box's centre, axes and sampled extremes. It is carried in the patch's geometry `g`: three
    numbers that `patchGeometryInto` writes (the angle bound, a and c), the brief's lean, so
    `select.ts`, which allocates by `PATCH_GEOMETRY_LENGTH`, is unchanged. Where H reaches c² ÷ a
    the normal keeps R05's chord (no level table approaches it).
  - _"Rounded up", as built._ The bound is an upper bound at each step rather than a figure
    rounded to a unit: Θ² through asin x ≤ x ÷ √(1 − x²), K = 1.155 ≥ 2 ÷ √3, |h| at its largest
    end, then the allowance for the `f64` arithmetic. The top along ν_c is argued from the critical
    points of x·ν_c on the regular offset surface, not from a convexity theorem, so it holds below
    the datum down to −c² ÷ a; the cut-off there, which keeps R05's chord, is tested on both sides.
  - _Its derivation_ (`normalMarginM`'s doc; checked by the science-checker, which re-derived ν″
    against finite differences and read both citations). For h > −c² ÷ a, X(d) = M·d + h·ν(d) is
    regular with normal ν(d), so x·ν_c over the sphere of directions has two critical points only,
    d_c (the greatest) and −d_c on the opposite face: the volume's top along ν_c is the centre
    vertex at the top of the range, sampled, and its bottom lies on the patch's boundary at an end
    of the range. Between neighbouring samples an edge is a great-circle arc of directions θ in
    [0, Θ], and the remainder of linear interpolation (Burden and Faires, 9th ed., §3.1, Theorem
    3.3) puts f(θ) = X(θ)·ν_c at most Θ² ÷ 8 · max|X″| below the lower sample, with
    |X″| ≤ a + (2 ÷ √3)|h| a² ÷ c² ((M·d)″ = −M·d; |ν″| ≤ (2 ÷ √3)|m′|² ÷ |m|², m = M⁻¹d).
  - _Deviation: the sagitta taken in the arc's angle, not the chord's length._ The entry has the
    chord's sagitta under a curvature bound ρ. A bound in the chord L needs a lower bound on the
    offset curves' radius of curvature and a separate argument that each arc is short (a curve of
    bounded curvature can wind); in the angle Θ it is one step, the interpolation remainder, with no
    condition on the arc. The two agree: on a sphere at the datum δ is R Θ² ÷ 8, the arc's own
    sagitta to O(Θ⁴), about L² ÷ (8R); on the spheroid the chord is at least 2c sin(Θ ÷ 2), so at
    the datum δ is about L² ÷ (8ρ) with ρ = c² ÷ a, `chordSagittaM`'s least radius of curvature
    (R05.T7.b's ruling). The radius-of-curvature bound the curvature form would need,
    (c − H a ÷ c)² ÷ (a + K H a² ÷ c²), is c² ÷ a at H = 0 and 6,259 km on an Earth at ±24.5 km.
  - _Not relying on the tops' chord._ The normal's margin reads no chord, so it holds for the bottom
    of the range without the brief's note that the tops' chord is the longer; the tangents' margin
    still takes the tops', as R05 built it.
  - _The figures of the bound_ (tests 5 and 6, WGS 84). The sagitta of a 566 m chord on an Earth is
    6.28 mm (a level-10 patch's mean spacing; 5.3–8.6 mm across a face as the warp's spacing
    varies, the science-checker's); ±24.5 km adds 0.45%. The allowance is 90.6 nm (91.0 nm at
    24.5 km). The sagitta is 20–33 nm at level 19, an Earth's finest, and from level 22 below an
    ulp of a (0.93 nm; 0.31–0.51 nm there), where the allowance alone pads the normal; the test
    holds levels 22–24 on every face with every vertex enclosed. The level-10 patch of test 5

    vertex, their projections, the box's centre and its half-extent) is under 30 ε (a + H);
    64 ε (a + H) more than doubles it. The margin tests hold each axis to 10 nm, finer than the
    margin at every level.

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule) (R10.T14.e)** (recorded, not ruled; each leaves the
  algorithm and the contracts as built).
  - _The boundary does not dip at all along the normal._ (M·d)″ = −M·d makes f″ =
    −M·d·ν_c + h ν″·ν_c, negative wherever M·d·ν_c > K |h| a² ÷ c², so along every edge arc the
    boundary bulges above its chord in ν_c and its lowest point is a sample. The science-checker
    puts the condition at H below about 0.49 a on an Earth-like figure and 0.36 a for c ≥ 0.9 a
    (every real planet; an Earth's H ÷ a is 0.004), and not for much flatter small bodies (H below
    0.17 a at c = 0.7 a). Test 1 sees it: no point past the samples at levels 0–15. The sagitta is
    kept as ruled; it costs millimetres.
  - _The boxes' remaining excess over the exact horizon_ (49 of the high setting's leaves at
    100 m, 1.02–1.35 across the table) is the box's flat top over its patch's curved edges, and the
    tangents' chord. Tighter volumes there (a box per edge, or the ring's own points against the
    horizon) are out of this task's scope; for T14.b, if the sizing needs it.
  - _Descent arcs now within two of D._ High's (0.49 → 0.93) and low's (no demand → 1.64), moved
    into `WITHIN_TWO`; high's orbit coast fell from 4.41 to no demand at all (still outside).
  - _High's replay pins rose by 3_ (884 → 887) as the boxes tightened: freed budget refines
    elsewhere under the replay's half-the-slots budget. Low's frames past its slots fell from 136
    to 107. T14.b measures on real bakes.
  - _A patch more in low's last two windows_ (68 → 69): the balance or the freed budget, not a
    looser box (every box is tighter or equal).
  - _Requests rose along the approach_ while its patches fell: 14,209 → 15,326 bake requests over
    its 48 frames (+7.9%) against 38,823 → 38,746 patches (−0.2%), and the orbit-and-secondary case
    under its budget asks 3 bakes where it asked 1. Worker time for T14.b.
  - _Skirts can hang below the box._ The mesh regime's `skirtDepthM`, and terrain skirts where
    `inheritedRangeInto` clamps a range to its level's low; before, the chord's slack covered them.
    Harmless: only culling and refinement read the box, and a skirt under a culled patch lies
    behind drawn surface.
  - _The box bounds the `f64` surface, not the GPU's `f32` vertices,_ which can sit a few parts in
    10⁸ of their distance from the camera outside it: far under a pixel, and culling only.

  - _What the trace found_ (hidden smoke, low, the NVIDIA driver's shader cache cold through a
    fresh `__GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_PATH`, a Chromium startup trace). At `b9515f03` the first phase's
    primary stopped for 1,250 ms at the hand-over and drew the terrain 2,483 ms after it. With the
    terrain lever alone the session's compile took 1,744 ms with a longest frame gap of 110 ms (the
    trace: `CreatePipelineAsyncEvent::InitializeImpl` on Dawn's workers, its
    `terrain-lit-face-differences` 1,581 ms), the terrain drew 0 ms after the hand-over, and the
    page still stopped 1,467–1,567 ms just before it: `DeviceBase::APICreateRenderPipeline` of
    `bodies:smoothMesh`, 1,547 ms on the GPU process's main thread. With both levers the same
    smoke's hand-over gap was 83 ms. The plan's text above carries the corrected attribution.
  - _The terrain lever._ `TerrainMaterialSet` (`TerrainMaterialSource`, `TerrainMaterialKind` `lit`,
    `depth` or `wire`, `terrainMaterialOf`, `sessionMaterials(setting, limits)`), made last in
    `TerrainSession`'s constructor (nothing after it can throw and leave it compiling, and it is
    before any pass). It compiles each material through `createMaterialAsync` against a mesh of the
    patches' own layout (`terrainMeshSpec`, named `terrain compile`, released after the compile),
    since the engine keys a material's pipelines by the mesh's layout, its target's format and its
    depth (pinned by the engine test "a material's pipelines by its mesh's layout"). A pass takes it
    as `TerrainPassOptions.materials`, draws with its handles and releases none; R05's spike shading
    keeps compiling its own. A path not compiled at the making is compiled at its first ask and
    kept; a refused compile is forgotten, so the next ask tries again; a compile a restore or the
    set's disposal overtook is released and rejects. At a restore it forgets the lost device's
    handles and compiles its setting again, its entries in place before a pass's resources rebuild,
    by R01's restore order, now stated in `RenderEngine.onRestored`'s contract (listeners in the
    order added) and held by a test. `TerrainSessionOptions.setting` is new and required (the
    launch's, through `useTerrainSession` and `ViewDisplay`; a change makes the session anew);
    `TerrainSession.compiled` and `compileStartedAtMs` are new. `gpu/resources.ts` gains
    `fittedTerrainLayout` (`null` where the device holds no layout, `terrainLayout` throwing as
    before) and `terrainMeshSpec`.
  - _The bodies' lever._ `RenderEngine.prepareMaterial(material, targets, meshes)` takes
    `PreparedTarget`s: a `RenderTargetFormat`, or `{ colour, depth }` for one output alone.
    `Drawing.preparePipeline` keeps the first pipeline made for a key, marks none pending for a
    `createMaterial` material, and leaves an asynchronous material's to `prepareMaterialPipeline`;
    the engine waits on a `createMaterial` material's compile check and prepares nothing of a broken
    one (call 2). `ResilientEngine` refuses a lost engine's material with `EngineUnavailable` and a
    released or foreign one with an `Error`. `LitBodyRenderer.#prepareRegimes` prepares
    `bodies:smoothMesh` on its patch and `bodies:disc` and `bodies:discLimb` on its quad for
    `{ colour: rgba16float, depth: true }` alone, the `bodies` and `discs` passes' output (call 1),
    as it makes its resources and at each restore (call 3: at `#create`, the opening's duplicate
    worker compile accepted); a failure other than `EngineUnavailable` is logged. R05's
    `pipelineShim` is not used (optional).
  - _The fakes, additive._ `CountingRenderEngine.compiles` (`RecordedCompile`) and `.prepares`
    (`RecordedPrepare`), refused asks too; its `createMaterialAsync` takes its targets and meshes;
    its `prepareMaterial` rejects with `EngineUnavailable` in a modelled loss and for a material
    not live. `FakeRenderEngine.prepared`. `EngineProbe.preparing`, and `ViewsProbe.preparations()`
    (`{ seen, inFlight, lastSettledAtMs }`), which `ProbedEngine.prepareMaterial` feeds.
  - _The run._ VIEW's opening runs from the run's start until the preparations its views made as
    they opened have settled (every view's drawer makes a `PhotorealRenderer`, so there are always
    some), recorded as `TerrainCheckRecord.opening` and not judged. The judged span runs from then
    to the teardown's choice of `PHASE TEST`: `TerrainCheckRecord.span`, the page's longest time
    between animation frames over it (`longestGapOutside`), outside the forced loss's restore and
    outside the run's own computation of each phase's record at its end, which held the main thread
    up to 558 ms in a diagnostic run (`harnessMs`, the time left out). Each session's phases start
    after `TerrainProbe.compiled`; each of `TerrainCheckRecord.sessions` holds its `madeAtMs` and
    its `compile`, `pending` or `ended` with its `compileMs`, `compiled` and `longestFrameGapMs`,
    timed from the session's own `compileStartedAtMs`, its window measured on the page's animation
    frames. `noStall` judges the span, each view's longest gap in each phase
    (`longestGapEndScriptS` new) and each session's compile window by `TERRAIN_GAP_LIMIT_MS`,
    saying which window a stall fell in; `framesDrawn` keeps the missed
    frames alone. `TERRAIN_CHECK_VERSION` 3 (also `phaseWindows`). The loss phase counts the fresh
    session's blocks from the mark taken before its `TERRAIN TEST` choice, since some can arrive
    during its compile.

    ruling asks no trace. Lean: the scene switch's rebuild of the views' renderers, whose first
    draws compile their materials again once the old ones are released (Dawn's cache holds weak
    references), which R01's warm-up would also remove.
  - _High's lit layout has no working fallback._ Where the high lit cache's offsets (1,286 slots ×
    101,400 B = 130,400,400 B) exceed a binding, `terrainLayout` falls back to `face-differences`,
    whose 1,908 slots' horizon map is 131,453,568 B, more than the offsets it replaces; so a device
    that cannot bind the offsets cannot bind the fallback either, and `terrainLayout` throws. Every
    adapter at WebGPU's default 134,217,728 B binds the offsets. The wireframe's 520 slots behave
    the same way (52.7 MB of offsets, 64.5 MB of heights on the fallback). For T14.b, which sizes
    the caches and the binding ceiling.
  - _Round 2's worst gaps sit at the first phase's configuration_ (high 250.1 ms, low 199.9 ms,
    between VIEW's opening and the first phase, where the primary first draws in the
    photorealistic style): not traced. Lean: the photorealistic renderer's other `createMaterial`
    materials (its sky's, its atmosphere's composite) drawing for the first time, R01's warm-up's
    to remove with VIEW's opening's.
  - _The run's own computation of its phases' records_ holds the page's main thread 14.9 s over a
    high run (1.8 s on low; the views probe's per-view filters over every frame of the run), left
    out of the judged span. For T14.b's runs, which time phases.
  - _Diagnostic smokes under a lane's 400 % CPU cap at a load near 4.5_ showed intermittent
    350–900 ms gaps whose main-thread frame time matched them (renderer JavaScript, not a
    compile), in no traced smoke and in neither cold run. Lean: the whole Electron tree, its six
    height workers included, throttled under the cap on a shared machine.

    - _The site._ Drawn by SplitMix64 from the seed (`descentProfile.ts`' now exported `splitMix64`

      index (none, and the spike refuses to fly, `NoLandingSite` ending it `TERRAIN NOT MEASURED`: a
      site elsewhere could fly its low pass over unsurveyed ground at the ceiling): a cell, a point
      uniform in its face square, an azimuth; then snapped to the centre vertex (32, 32) of the
      finest patch holding it, computed from the cell's (s, t) clamped inside the cell, so that it
      cannot slip past a cell's edge. A candidate whose floors refuse the profile gives way to the
      next draw; the bakes are kept across attempts.
    - _The site height_ is that vertex's own-level height in the finest bake: on R05's diagonal,
      since the vertex lies on every triangle it touches. `SITE ELEVATION` states the workers'
      reading there (`groundReadout`'s `reading.elevationM` and `elevationSigmaM`,
      `surveyed_reading`'s) in `ELEVATION`'s form, Missing until answered; the slant range from 1 km
      above is the query.
    - _The floors._ A stretch whose patches are all wholly surveyed takes its baked maximum plus ε_n
      from the workers' table; a stretch any of whose patches has an unsurveyed cell under it takes
      the body-wide ceiling, unbaked (`offSurveyCeilingM`: the table's highest over its rows plus
      the header's realised relief and a metre, `reading.rs`' `ceiling_m`), which bounds all ground
      at every level, so the floor there is the ceiling itself.
    - _σ_n._ The workers' table carries no σ_n, so `omittedSigmaM` is +∞ at every level: the
      calibrated count min(ε_n, 4σ_n) is the hard one. Nothing serialises it.

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule) (R10.T14.c)** (recorded, not ruled; each leaves the
  algorithm and the contracts as built).
  - _Other craft at the present, bodies at their emission_ (decision-r10-t14c-leans, "Seen, not
    ruled" 1). A craft other than the own ship is placed at the scene's time and every body but the
    local one where it is seen, so a contact against a moon seen across light time τ stands off by
    about |V_M − V_obs| τ: 66.8 m for a craft at Phobos seen from Mars, beyond r_g. Unreachable
    today (the server's craft source is `NoCraft`; kept scenes have no light time). Owner: the plan
    that first serves craft, with decision-r10-ship-frame's finding 2.
  - _A craft at rest over a coarse bake_ (2). Its read ground, perhaps a wholly surveyed bake's 17 ×
    17 grid two levels coarser, can lie more than r_g below it, and it is then no contact until the
    view's own selection refines under it; harmless in the picture (wherever the craft spans a pixel
    the drawn ground is within τ pixels). The lever: judge "grounded" on the read clearance less the
    read bake's stated bound. Owner: R11, once landed craft are seen from afar.
  - _"Descending" over coarse bakes may start a forced region late_ (3), by up to the read bake's
    error over the closing speed; `FORCED_REGION_RESIDENCY_S` stays provisional. Owner: T14.b, which
    records the region's residency before contact on this run.
  - _The lit and wire passes of one body judge contacts on their own resident sets_ (4), and may
    place a contact differently for a frame or two. The lever: the finer of the two grounds. Owner:
    T14.b, if its two-style runs show it.
  - _R05's table is Earth's_ (5). The orbit coast is flown at 7.67 km/s at 400 km: 5.1 times the
    Moon-like world's circular speed there (1.51 km/s) and 3.6 times its escape speed (2.14 km/s);
    the script is not Keplerian by R05's design, and the cache's peaks are set below 4 km, so the
    run keeps the table. The lever: the high segments' speeds scaled by the body's circular speed.
    Owner: T14.b's record.
  - _R05's rule 4 cannot refuse a finite floor._ Probing the profile with single floors up to 10⁷ m
    and 800 random patterns up to 10⁵ m, every one was cleared by the lifts; `DescentUnclearable`
    appeared only near 10²⁰ m, where a double's step swallows the lift, so the spike's
    `DESCENT REFUSED` and the next-candidate path are reached in tests only by such a floor or a
    non-finite one. Owner: R05's profile (decision-r05-descent-clearance), for main.
  - _The trace's first boundary flakes under load._ One hidden smoke of each world failed with "the
    trace's start (or cycle at 3 s) was still pending at the boundary" (2026-10-20, 19:02 and 19:05,
    1-minute load about 12–15, with r10-compile's runs about); the test planet's passed at
    `b9515f03` itself minutes later and on this tree after it, and the terrain world's passed on its
    next run (99, 113 and 171 frames matched). Owner: R05's harness (the smoke's 3 s windows), for
    T14.b's runs.
  - _Untimed passes are not counted over a generated world_ (`passesSubmitted` `null`): neither the
    engine nor the drawer counts a frame's passes, and a drawer's frame spans many resolves. The
    proposal: count the passes per resolve in the spike's device shim (`spikeDeviceWrapper`). Owner:
    T14.b.
  - _The spike's seams on the session's pass_: `onSelect` misses each pass's first selection (made
    in the step that makes the pass), and `onPatch`'s `baked` is the pass's residency, a bake the
    cache refuses uncounted. Owner: T14.b, if its figures need them.
  - _`--vertex-path` and `--normals` are refused over a generated world_: the session's passes take
    the setting's own terrain (`#makePass`). Owner: T14.b, if it measures a variant.
  - _The terrain readout is not run on the spike_ (decision-r10-t14c-guide, Q1): `VIEW`'s primary
    runs it at 4 Hz on the height workers, so T14.b's worker-time figures state that they exclude
    it, or T14.b adds it.

    `qualitySetting.ts`, `cacheBudget.ts` and `slotLayout.ts`, `terrainWireSelection.test.ts`'
    stale module remark (ruling 6(a)), and the measurements' README. The four results files under
    `docs/measurements/descent-spike/`. No wire, protocol, DTO, golden, generator version or Rust
    change. Main's two test fixes
    (`DescentSpike.test.tsx`'s missing site elevation waits for the measuring line to go;
    `bodyDescent.test.ts`' refusal over every candidate takes the harness's patience) ride in the
    harness's second commit.
  - _The option._ `--sizes on|off`, off by default and absent from the launch, the run's options and
    the summary when off, so that every other run and file is as before (T14.c's tests unedited);
    refused with `--world test-planet`. On, over a generated world:
    - _The counts_ (`PassSizeCounter`, ruling §2): at each pass's first selection in each whole
      second of script time, five unbudgeted re-selections of the pass's own input
      (`TerrainPass.observe`'s `onSelect`), over the counter's own shallow copy of the planet, so
      that `select.ts`' memo and the pass's selection are untouched (tested frame for frame on two
      real passes): F at the pass's margins; F₀ at none; AR with every view `allRound`; F′ and AR′
      with `occluderHeightM` at the diagnostic depth. A view's count is the leaves its bit marks,
      forced leaves left out; the forced region is counted once.
    - _`select.ts`' options_, counting only, never set by the pass: `ViewSelectionInput.allRound`
      (no frustum planes, its horizon alone culling) and `SelectionInput.occluderHeightM` (in place
      of `lowestHeightM` in every view's horizon, the boxes untouched). Absent, every selection is as
      before, bit for bit (`select.test.ts`' digests unedited). On the count model's premise planet
      an all-round view counts 1.000–1.016 times `patchCountModel`'s `allRound` on the boxes (low at
      100 km 196 against 193, held to [0.99, 1.02]).
    - _The second view_ (§4): the craft instrument at its chase pose is a `SpikeSessionView` under
      `instrumentViewId(1)` (`InstrumentSlot` is 1 or 2, so not the ruling's 0), `secondary` (weight
      0.25), in the main view's style on high and the wireframe on low's photorealistic run; the
      orbit instrument stays R02's. Its viewport is the craft stage's: 376 × 140 px on high and
      80 × 140 px on low (571 and 275 px wide for its first frame). The views are found in a
      selection's input by weight, then viewport.
    - _The bake clock_ (§6(c)): each bake's post to reply and an estimate of the worker's own time
      (the reply less the later of its post and the worker's previous reply of any kind), from the
      flight's first frame; baked less resident is "never resident".
    - _The readout_ (§6(f)): `VIEW`'s `GroundReadouts` on the main view at 250 ms, its answers not
      shown, its guards' `failComputation` counted and never passed on, so that the measurement's
      readout cannot end a run (none was called in the four runs).
    - _Memory and the binding_ (§6(d), §6(g)): the session's `memory()` at 1 Hz; each cache's
      allocation; the engine's allocations by category (`RenderEngine.onAllocation`), the cascades
      as built from its `shadows` peak (R10.T9.b landed before the runs); the adapter's reported,
      the engine's requested and the device's `maxStorageBufferBindingSize` and each cache's binding
      ceiling there and at WebGPU's default; the 1-minute load at the start, each minute and the
      end. These sit in the `sizes` block, not the run block, so that no other run's file gains a
      field (a deviation from the ruling's "run block adds").
    - _The results_ (§6(g)): an optional `sizes` block (`RESULTS_VERSION` stays 6; files without it
      read as before) and a "Sizes" section in the summary. A malformed block is written beside the
      results as `<name>-sizes-rejected.json` rather than losing the run (none was). The 1 Hz
      columns keep the moment, each view's five counts, the forced region and its residency, the
      slots in use and the shares' numerators; the pass's own counts are kept by segment. Formatted,
      the four files are 271–323 kB.
  - _Deviations from the ruling's wording._ The diagnostic depth's resident term walks the resident
    patches over the leaves of F, AR and the pass's own selection (`PatchCache` has no public walk
    of its patches), not every resident bake; a resident patch over none of them is not read. The
    peaks' height is the craft's over its stretch's floor (`DescentPose.heightAboveFloorM`), a lower
    bound of its height above the ground beneath. The forced region's lead is timed to touchdown
    (the first frame down to the last segment's end), the session's contact rule firing in the very
    step that first selects the forced patches; that first frame is recorded beside it. The
    stand-in share is standing in ÷ selected. Per-segment figures are taken on every run. The
    horizon A/B is by the whole run, not per segment (rulings 6(b) and the constants' item 8): the
    results keep each pass's percentiles by label for the whole run.

    (`terrainShipBodyFixedM`, `terrainShipGround`, `shipAttitude`), and its `sceneS = 60 tS` only
    turns the moon, moves the sun and sets the clock, so the scene's clock never reaches selection:
    a 1 s/s scene flies the same track and selects the same patches, and T11's attribution of the
    factor to the clock is corrected. The spike's 1 s/s logs split it instead:
    - the motion margin: F ÷ F₀ at 1.00–1.03 at the peaks (1.15 at most, low's second view);
    - the bound ratio: the moon's level table has k_n = ε_n P₀ ÷ e_n of 49 at L0, 270–540 at
      L4–L16 (the hard bound: the workers' table carries no σ_n, so `omittedSigmaM` is +∞), against
      the count model's k₀ = 5 and R05's golden table's about 15;
    - the boxes: at F's peak the seen leaves' boxes stand (median) 44 km at L7, 26 km at L8, 15 km
      at L9 and 7.2 km at L10, R09's remaining reach (T8.d's 3.9 times the realised relief); the
      largest at L13–L17 are 1.6–11.4 km over the runs, and low's starved instrument's 130–168 km at

    - T14.a's factors beside them: the margin's cap ×1.15–1.22, k₀ = 15 ×3.5–6.7 and the relief
      ×4.7–9.5.

  - _The binding's clamp_ (§4; T14.d's "High's lit layout has no working fallback"). `fitLayout`
    (`gpu/resources.ts`) keeps the layout as before where every storage field binds at the
    setting's own path and slot count
    (within min(`maxStorageBufferBindingSize`, `maxBufferSize`), by `cacheBudget.ts`'
    `bindingCeilingSlots`); otherwise it takes `face-differences` at the same slot count
    (decisions-r06-r07 item 7's "keeping the slot budget": as built it re-derived the count from
    the bytes, taking high lit from 1,286 to 1,908 slots on a lesser device, and the draw budget
    with it) and clamps the count to that path's binding ceiling, `fallback: "binding-limit"` and
    the new `requestedSlotCount` recording it. It refuses only where fewer than six slots (the
    roots, `MIN_SLOTS`) bind on `face-differences`, or the atlas refuses. As held, the clamp never
    engages at the RTX 3080's limits or at WebGPU's defaults (1,286 ≤ 1,323, 520 ≤ 1,323,
    422 ≤ 1,948): it makes T14.d's dead fallback work (high lit at its 1,286 slots on a
    128,000,000 B binding keeps them on `face-differences`, where it threw) and the re-size a
    constants-only change. One move: R05's spike shading on high at WebGPU's default limits keeps
    its 1,962 slots on `face-differences`, where it took 3,904. `materialSet.test.ts`' bindings for
    each refused path are re-chosen (at 10⁸ B high's lit, depth and shadow materials now take
    `face-differences` and the wireframe `baked-offsets`). The spike's binding block carries each
    cache's `slotCount` and an optional `layout` holding its `requestedSlotCount` and `fallback`,
    optional so that the four results files read unedited.

  - _The caches hold a seventh of the hard bound's demand_ (decision-r10-t14b-constants §6). Low
    lit 2,996 slots measured against 422 held (×7.1), high lit 8,666 against 1,286 (×6.7), the
    wireframe 3,764 and low's two views 3,623 against 520 (×7.2, ×7.0): neither 64 MiB nor about
    400 MB holds the as-built selection's demand on a generated world. Levers: R10.T4.b's
    min(hard, 4σ) (×2–3); R09's (ii) and decision-r09-t8d-reach §5's per-view occluder, for the tall
    boxes; a draw budget apart from the slots; the pool's per-pass share (below); bake throughput
    (below). The re-size above is pre-ruled.
  - _The A/B's price on the per-view sum_ (§8 (a)): 6.8% (high photorealistic) and 13.3% (high
    wireframe, told to main), all of it the second view's frustum peak; 0% on the adopted union
    form, which the 10% line reads, and AR′ = AR everywhere, so the remaining looseness is the
    boxes'. Lever: decision-r09-t8d-reach §5's (ii); a per-view occluder from the resident bakes'
    lows.
  - _"Ever resident" is met only at 190 km_ (§8 (b)), where AR∪ is a few coarse patches. Read at
    AR∪'s peak the cap is 0.28–0.32 and high's peak share 11%: the set was never resident in the
    flare on any run. The harness reports both; no code change.
  - _The canvases are smaller than the setting's rows_ (§8 (c)): the main view's hidden canvas is
    the stage beside the instruments, 1,398 × 793 px on high and 806 × 431 on low, not 1,080 and
    720 rows, so a τ-limited count could rise by up to (1080 ÷ 793)² ≈ 1.9 and (720 ÷ 431)² ≈ 2.8
    on a full-height view: the rule's figures and the measured ÷ model ratios are lower bounds. The
    re-size takes the nominal rows.
  - _The wireframe's share_ (§8 (d)): r, wireframe ÷ high lit, is 0.43 in F∪ and 0.44 in AR∪ (high
    wireframe against high photorealistic), far above the model's 0.13–0.19 and τ⁻² = 0.0625: on
    this world the boxes and the horizon govern, not τ. The brainstorm's "about a fifth" is not
    edited; it waits on R10.T4.b. `terrainWireSelection.test.ts` keeps its bracket.

    wireframe pass attached at about 1,050 s with nothing resident, drew nothing through the
    approach and flare (432.5 patches missing on average) and almost nothing until the vertical
    descent, while the lit pass saturated the pool; its selection fell to 2 patches in the low fast
    pass (the cause not traced: its boxes stand 130–168 km tall at every level from L4, nothing
    resident tightening them); the two passes' forced sets differed in 6,517 of 14,896 frames
    (T14.c's finding 4). Not a blocker: the instrument's own `TERRAIN: STREAMING` annunciates it
    (R10.T16.c). Lever: a per-pass share of the pool, an empty pass's coarsest levels served first.
  - _The terrain row reads `terrain shadows` alone_ (§8 (f)): high's terrain "pass" is 3.24 ms at
    p95 while the lit draws sit in `bodies` (4.30 ms), and low shows "no timed terrain pass", so the
    spike's terrain row misses the terrain's own draws over a generated world. Lever: time the
    terrain's draws in `bodies` apart.

    p50 100–420 ms, 6–34% never resident, at a run's load of 2.5–14. Levers: R09's fused interpolant
    (T6.a's 40 ms), the worker count, decision-r10-t14b-measure 6(c)'s eviction in place of rebakes.
  - _The forced region_ (§8 (h)): its lead before touchdown was 23–32 s with every forced patch
    resident at touchdown, though low's "all resident" lapsed after 1,168–1,169 s as new forced
    patches entered. No forced insert can have been refused: the forced pins peaked at 108 against
    422–1,286 slots, and the cache evicts any unforced patch before refusing one.
    `FORCED_REGION_RESIDENCY_S` stays as it is.

    high setting's frustum set. No cache size makes a turn cheap; only the bound does.

    `reading`, `material`) to the bit: the reading at a `SlopeBaseline`, a member of
    `SLOPE_BASELINES` checked at the boundary since `surveyed_reading` panics on another
    (decision-r10-t12-leans §1); the material; the capacity, `bearing_capacity_on_slope` at the
    header's gravity under the pad on the RMS slope over the fixed 2 m (`CAPACITY_SLOPE_BASELINE`)
    whatever the baseline, and none under a pad not finite and positive; the month's temperature and
    the friction (§6). A foot outside the survey reads `NotSurveyed`. The wasm `groundReadout` takes
    flat arguments, the season as `number | undefined` and refuses a non-finite one with a `JsError`,
    so no NaN reaches `month_at`; `GroundReadoutAnswer` holds the answer itself. On the client: the
    `ground-readout` request and its two replies (the reading types moved from `heightBake.ts` to
    `messages.ts`, against an import cycle); `HeightWorkerPool.groundReadout` beside `classMap`,
    over a discriminated pending query whose `receive` is exhaustive; and
    `TerrainSession.groundReadout(view, body, sight, time, options)`, async, with the baseline
    typed `SlopeBaselineM`, `null` once disposed, for a body not wanted, with no seed or field held,
    or for a view it holds no report of. The view enters at the session, not at the pool's query,
    which takes a line of sight alone (§3).

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule) (T12's back end)** (recorded, not ruled; each leaves the
  algorithm and the contracts as built).
  1. _A readout's own figures across targets._ The temperature, friction and capacity of one
     readout are compared on one target only; each is plain IEEE arithmetic over inputs that
     goldens pin (`months.golden`, `table.golden`, `bearing_on_slope.golden`). A small worker
     golden of a glacier point's readout either side of a month's edge would pin them across
     targets (the determinism audit's lever).
  2. _The season's orbit past its record's `valid_until`._ The session never asks the record again,
     so a long session's month comes from elements past their range: negligible for the month.
  3. _The line of sight's raw fields._ The query types the baseline and the season but carries the
     origin, direction and reach as raw values that `sight_of` checks and `slant_range` asserts
     again; a checked sight type would end its `# Panics`.
  4. _The rounding's remaining overstatement._ "Never down" still rounds a figure up a whole step
     (a range's σ of 0.31 km reads `± 0.4 km`).
  5. _Vesić's inclination factors_ were not read in a primary here (the science check could not
     reach Vesić 1975 or EM 1110-1-1905); the slope ruling read them.

  4. At a ratio of 1 and 80%, the upper ticks' ends come about 1.8 px from the selection bracket's

- **`VIEW`'s room, ruled (decision-r10-view-block-room).** The floor is 80 × 45 rem (1280 × 720 at
  100%, 1920 × 1080 at 150%); a 1280 × 720 window at 125% or 150% is below it. Stated limits: at
  the floor beside an open instrument the primary holds back its terrain lines and, in `CHASE`,
  scrolls a line or two of `POSITION` to `METER`, the `EXPOSURE` line included; only one wireframe
  instrument stands over terrain at the floor; below the floor the upper plate may scroll whole,
  held at its foot.
- **Deviations in R10.T12.b, as built** (2026-10-20; decision-r10-view-block-room).
  - _Files._ Beyond the entry's list, all under `apps/hyperion/src/renderer/src/`:
    `displays/view/viewRoom.ts` (the pure decision, `viewRoom`, with `roomToOpen` in place of
    `ViewDisplay.tsx`'s `roomForSlot`, `lowerYieldLine` and `LowerPlatePart`),
    `displays/view/plateMeasures.ts` (the plates as laid out), `displays/view/ViewRoomSizers.tsx`
    (the hidden copies), `displays/view/ViewLowerPlate.tsx`, `displays/view/InstrumentStub.tsx`,
    `view/terrain/poseInterval.ts` (one interval for a pose), `displays/view/useInstruments.ts`
    (each instrument's published interval and the holder), `view/terrain/frameTerrain.ts` (the
    holder on `ViewTerrainInput` and `WireframeTerrainInput`) and `test/viewDisplayHarness.tsx`
    (a plate's parts and the sizers laid out as nothing, the stub's size). `InstrumentView.tsx`
    gains no held state of its own: a held slot's `InstrumentView` is not rendered.
  - _How it is decided._ One pure function of the plates' heights at the stage's full width and
    beside the slots, the stage's size, the slots' last standing heights and the room decided
    before (the hysteresis), re-run at each render. The heights are measured after each render:
    the live upper plate, which always holds all its lines and only clips them while it scrolls
    (its lines measured at the scroll's width while it scrolls); and hidden, `aria-hidden` copies
    (`ViewRoomSizers`) for what is not shown: the lower plate's three forms at its tallest (whole,
    the readout given way, the survey given way too) at the live plates' width, and, only while
    the slots are held for the plates (step 4), both plates beside where the slots would stand,
    the copy's lines before `STARS` set at a scroll bar's width so that they are reckoned as tall
    as they would stand scrolled. Beside standing slots the live plates stand for the full width
    too, a narrower and so a taller reckoning, until the plates take the full width and are
    measured there. So no decision feeds back on what it measures but through a cut.
  - _A line to spare_ is one label row, 0.875 rem at B612's 1.25 line height, 1.094 rem
    (`LINE_SPARE_REM`, the ruling's "about 1.09 rem"): a part that gave way returns, a held slot
    returns, and slots held for the plates return once beside them the plates would stand by step
    3, each with it to spare. A slot just opened is not a return: it stands where it fits, as its
    `OPEN` was given (`roomToOpen`, which keeps `roomForSlot`'s rule with the slots that stand
    reckoned, a stub as its stub and a held slot as nothing, and holds `OPEN` back where a slot
    already stands and the plates would not stand beside a second by step 3; with no slot open
    nothing beside a slot is measured, so an `OPEN` that trips step 4 opens the slot held, its row
    saying so).
  - _The hysteresis holds at one stage._ A room sets the next one's hysteresis only where both
    were decided at the same stage (its size to half a pixel, at the same interface scale) from
    plates measured there (`ViewRoom.basis`); after a resize or a change of interface scale the
    room is decided afresh, since no statement came or went (beyond the text, from the lane's
    tests: at 1280 × 720 at 100% both slots stand with 9 px to spare, and a line's margin would
    have kept `INSTRUMENT 2` as its stub after 150% and back, against §11's "the slot returns as it
    was"). `INSTRUMENT 2` held whole returns as its stub only with a line to spare, as a stub
    returns whole, so that it does not change between the two as `INSTRUMENT 1`'s statements come
    and go.
  - _Within a step_ the lines the scroll keeps in view follow the room at once; only a return to a
    step before asks a line to spare. So the scroll may grow or shrink by a line as a statement
    comes and goes, and its lines are always reached by scrolling.
  - _Step 4 at the full width._ Once the slots are held for the plates, the plates are decided again
    at the stage's full width, from step 0, the line to spare counted from the step decided beside
    the slots: a part that gave way beside the slots stands again wherever the full width holds it.
  - _Steps 5 and 6 are not gated by the window's size._ They apply wherever steps 1 to 4 do not
    hold the plates, which the design expects, and the looks found, only below the floor; gated,
    the alternative would be a cut, which the ruling forbids at every size. Step 6 keeps the plate's
    `VIEW` line above its scroll, which takes everything under it, with its position line beneath:
    "the whole upper plate scrolls" is read as the plate's body, the `VIEW` line naming the plate.
  - _The scrolling parts_ are `section`s, regions only while they scroll and are named:
    `PRIMARY lines` for the lines before `STARS`, `PRIMARY label block` for everything under the
    `VIEW` line, each with the default scroll bar and its position line in `.list-position`'s form,
    as the readouts' scrolls are (`BodyReadout`'s `Readings`).
  - _The focus_ (beyond the text; the UX review). Where a render takes away the element over the
    stage that last held the focus, a held or returning slot's canvas, the stub, or a scroll that
    ended with its tab stop, the focus goes to the `PRIMARY` view's canvas, never to the page,
    where no ring would show.
  - _A held slot_ is not drawn: its `InstrumentView` is not rendered, so its canvas, its drawer
    and its terrain view go, it leaves the budgets' specs, its camera leaves the server's scene
    while held (its frames report it again as it returns) and its held flight keys are released;
    its camera, style and target stay in `useInstruments`. It is reckoned at its height as it last
    stood whole, in rem, so that a scale change reckons it at the new scale. It is not the
    `CONTROLS` view while held: its `CONTROLS` button is held back by the no-room line, the side
    column reads `PRIMARY`, and the operator's choice returns with the slot (the lane's choice;
    acting on a view that is not drawn would change it unseen). Its statements are not computed
    while it is not drawn, so it returns once the room about it grows by its height as it stood and
    a line (a larger stage, or the other slot shorter or closed), not when its own statements would
    have cleared. `INSTRUMENT 2` is held first: its stub while `INSTRUMENT 1` stands, held whole
    where even the stub does not fit; where `INSTRUMENT 1` cannot stand, `INSTRUMENT 2` alone may
    stand in its corner. The stub's `CLOSE` gives the focus to the `PRIMARY` view's canvas, since
    it goes with the slot.
  - _The `INSTRUMENTS` panel._ One line,
    `NOT AVAILABLE: no room for INSTRUMENT 1 and INSTRUMENT 2 at this window size`, names every
    slot the stage has no room for: a closed one's `OPEN` held back, and an open one held, as its
    stub or whole; it describes their `OPEN` and the held ones' `CONTROLS`. While the panel is folded, the line naming the slots held whole stands under its
    own disclosure row, its title (the lane's reading of "under the disclosure row"; a stub states
    its reason on the stage itself).
  - _The plates' width_ is an explicit `view-label--beside` class from the room in place of the
    `.view__overlay:has(.view-instrument)` rule, at the same `calc(100% - 36.5rem)`, so that the
    sizers' copies and the live plates take one width by one rule.
  - _One interval for a pose_ (`PoseIntervals`). A view whose camera, body-fixed, stands within
    1 m (`POSE_TOLERANCE_M`) of a point at which another view stated its interval, over the body
    its camera stands lowest over, takes that interval where it was stated in the same primary
    frame, and else steps its hysteresis from the latest interval held at that point, its own or
    another's, so that its own newer interval is never stepped back from another's older one (a
    still camera's case, found by the lane's tests); elsewhere, from its own. A view whose frame
    states none (a photorealistic frame, no body's terrain) leaves the holder, which the
    primary's redraw effect makes and gives the instruments' frames. The primary draws first in a
    frame, so instruments at its pose take its interval. Beyond the text: the 4 Hz
    publish moves to a frame the 30 Hz instruments draw in too (at most 16.7 ms later at a 60 Hz
    primary), so that every block changes interval in the same render.
  - _The lower plate's interface_, for R10.T12's label-block commit: `ViewStage`'s `lowerParts`
    (`NO_LOWER_PARTS` until then), a list of `LowerPlatePart`s in the guide's order, each a
    `state` line (never yields) or a `survey`, `datum` or `readout` part with its `node` and its
    `tallest` node (every reading Estimated, stale and `GRAZING`, `DATUM` with `SEA LEVEL`), each

    tripod and the `GROUND AT LINE OF SIGHT` note.

    (decision-r10-view-block-room, "Seen" item 1). _Deferred by R10.T12.a (decision-r10-t12a-scope
    §7): a later desktop pass; the label rule moves nothing at the floor alone._

  - _Files._ Beyond the entry's list, all under `apps/hyperion/src/renderer/src/`:
